evidence.snippet: CA II deficiency is the paradigm OPT featuring failure of osteoclasts to resorb bone due to inability to acidify their pericellular milieu.
evidence.explanation: The same sentence carries the next step as well: failed acidification is given as the reason resorption fails.

edges/6.description: Hydroxyapatite dissolution is acid-dependent, so a lacuna that is not acidified does not release bone mineral.

evidence.snippet: Other features include developmental delay, short stature, cognitive defects, and a history of multiple fractures by adolescence.
evidence.explanation: Records repeated fracture as a consequence of the skeletal disease.

edges/11.description: Dense bone in this disease is brittle rather than strong, and fracture is a presenting feature.

evidence.snippet: Globes and retinae were normal, but optic nerve involvement was present in 23/46 eyes and was variable in severity, random in occurrence and statistically correlated with degree of optic canal narrowing.
evidence.explanation: The cohort supports an association between canal narrowing and optic nerve involvement; it does not experimentally exclude all primary neural injury.

edges/12.description: Compression of the optic nerve within a narrowed bony canal.

evidence.snippet: This condition leads to specific craniofacial dysmorphisms associated with upper airway obstruction that may result in obstructive sleep apnea.
evidence.explanation: States the craniofacial-to-airway-obstruction step for CA II deficiency specifically.

evidence.snippet: In CA II deficiency, OPT is uniquely accompanied by renal tubular acidosis (RTA) of proximal, distal, or combined type featuring hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis, rarely with hypokalemia and paralysis.
evidence.explanation: Names the tubular defect and the systemic acid-base consequence it produces, together with the range of tubular segments involved.

evidence.snippet: In CA II deficiency, OPT is uniquely accompanied by renal tubular acidosis (RTA) of proximal, distal, or combined type featuring hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis, rarely with hypokalemia and paralysis.
evidence.explanation: Names the tubular defect and the systemic acid-base consequence it produces, together with the range of tubular segments involved.

evidence.snippet: With one exception, all patients with osteopetrosis and renal tubular acidosis examined have proven to have CA II deficiency. All CA II-deficient patients analyzed have been found to have mutations in the CA2 gene.
evidence.explanation: The bidirectional gene-disease specificity statement, and the reason this is curated as a single disease rather than a grouping.

evidence.snippet: Segregation analysis of the molecular marker and chromosomes in cell hybrids indicated a clear correlation between the presence of chromosome 8 and the human CA II gene (CA2).
evidence.explanation: Somatic cell hybrid mapping of CA2 to chromosome 8, the step that made molecular diagnosis possible.

evidence.snippet: These mutations were scattered over the genome from exon 2 to 7.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that pathogenic variants are distributed across the gene rather than clustering in one domain, which is why diagnostic sequencing covers all seven exons.

evidence.snippet: Free energy dynamics of tertiary structure models of CA2 mutants with DUET, mCSM, and SDM based consensus methods predicted only 50% of the variants as destabilizing.
evidence.explanation: Bounds what in silico prediction can do for the missense class: consensus free-energy methods called only half of already-known disease-causing CA2 missense variants destabilizing, so a non-destabilizing prediction is not evidence against pathogenicity in this gene.

evidence.snippet: Superimposition of native and mutant CA2 models revealed the minor structural fluctuations at the amino acid residue level but not at the whole protein structure level.
evidence.explanation: Gives the reason the free-energy methods underperform: the perturbation is residue-local rather than global, which is the signal whole-protein stability scores are least able to see.

genes/0.notes: CA2 encodes cytosolic carbonic anhydrase II. Splice-site, nonsense, frameshift and missense variants have been reported. Homozygous and compound-heterozygous genotypes occur. A predicted truncation or splice disruption does not by itself demonstrate absent protein in every tissue; His107Tyr retains residual activity in recombinant assays. Coexistent osteopetrosis and renal tubular acidosis can also result from coinherited defects in other genes.

evidence.snippet: Several mouse models of CA II deficiency have shown growth hormone deficiency, yet currently there is no standard pharmacologic therapy for patients.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that no pharmacologic therapy is standardised for this disease - the reason alkali therapy is described here as the mainstay for one arm rather than as a protocol.

evidence.snippet: Oral therapy with sodium bicarbonate and potassium citrate was started with improvement of blood acidosis (Table 1) and blood HCO3-.
evidence.explanation: Direct clinical response supports correction of acidosis; it does not establish normalization of all disease manifestations.

treatments/0.description: Oral bicarbonate or citrate treats the acid-base disturbance. In the child reported with obstructive sleep apnea, sodium bicarbonate and potassium citrate improved blood acidosis and bicarbonate. Earlier treatment was proposed to explain milder outcomes in a separate cohort, but that comparison does not establish a disease-modifying neurological effect.

evidence.snippet: Oral therapy with sodium bicarbonate and potassium citrate was started with improvement of blood acidosis (Table 1) and blood HCO3-.
evidence.explanation: Direct clinical response supports correction of acidosis; it does not establish normalization of all disease manifestations.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Exogenous alkali can improve systemic acidosis without correcting the underlying genotype.

evidence.snippet: Post-transplantation evaluation at 2 and 3 years demonstrates histologic and radiologic resolution of their osteopetrosis with stabilization of hearing and vision.
evidence.explanation: Documents resolution of the skeletal disease after transplantation.

evidence.snippet: He Engrafted on day +13, and 95% chimerism was achieved.
evidence.explanation: A recent worked case with matched related donor engraftment, confirming feasibility in this specific genotype.

evidence.snippet: Although CA II deficiency is an "osteoclast-rich" OPT, and therefore transplantation of healthy osteoclasts can improve the skeletal disease, the RTA and central nervous system difficulties persist.
evidence.explanation: The review summarizes skeletal improvement with persistent renal and central nervous system difficulties; it does not establish that every extra-skeletal outcome is unchanged.

evidence.snippet: Both children remain developmentally delayed and continue to have RTA, and the older child has now developed cerebral calcification.
evidence.explanation: Documents persistent extra-skeletal findings despite skeletal response.

evidence.snippet: He is currently doing well without immunosuppressive therapy, now 12 months post HSCT, with normal calcium level and improving visual quality and FISH analysis revealed complete donor chimerism.
evidence.explanation: The later report provides twelve-month clinical and chimerism outcomes, not proof of lifelong multisystem cure.

treatments/1.description: Allogeneic transplantation supplies donor hematopoietic precursors and can resolve osteopetrosis. In two related Irish families, two transplanted children had histological and radiographic skeletal improvement with stabilized hearing and vision at two and three years. Renal tubular acidosis and developmental delay persisted; the older transplanted child subsequently developed cerebral calcification. The authors suggested delayed calcification, which is distinct from proving neurological correction or proving that transplantation has no cerebral effect. A later Iranian child had improving vision and complete donor chimerism at twelve months. These small reports do not establish routine use for every patient.

evidence.snippet: Allogeneic bone marrow stem cell replacement cures the osteoclast component of CAII deficiency and retards the development of cerebral calcification, but it appears to have little or no effect on the renal lesions.
evidence.explanation: States precisely which arm the transplant corrects and which it does not, which is what makes this an arm-specific mechanism link.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Donor hematopoietic precursors can restore the osteoclast lineage; skeletal histology and imaging support correction of bone disease rather than a direct measurement of lacunar pH.

evidence.snippet: Herein we report a case of osteopetrosis with RTA associated with severe OSAS successfully treated with continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP).
evidence.explanation: The single report of CPAP use in this disease.

treatments/2.description: CPAP for craniofacial obstructive sleep apnea. Reported in a single child in whom adherence built up gradually from a minimal starting pressure. Relevant because the airway obstruction in this disease is skeletal in origin, so adenotonsillectomy alone may not resolve it - in the reported family the twin had a severe respiratory complication after that surgery.

evidence.snippet: Globes and retinae were normal, but optic nerve involvement was present in 23/46 eyes and was variable in severity, random in occurrence and statistically correlated with degree of optic canal narrowing
evidence.explanation: The case for surveillance rather than symptom-driven referral: half of eyes affected, occurrence random so not predictable from the rest of the phenotype, and a measurable bony parameter that tracks it.

evidence.snippet: Optic nerve atrophy was observed in 22.2 %, while brain calcifications were present in 70.0 % of cases.
evidence.explanation: Frequency of optic nerve atrophy in a consecutive pediatric series, which is the prevalence that justifies routine rather than selective assessment.

evidence.snippet: Two children, one from each family, have undergone allogeneic bone marrow transplantation because of severe progressive visual and hearing loss.
evidence.explanation: Surveillance has a consequence here: detected progressive visual loss was the stated indication for escalating to transplantation in these families.

evidence.snippet: Follow-up brain imaging may not aid in prognosis or severity assessment, highlighting the need for further research.
evidence.explanation: Scopes the surveillance claim to the eye. The same series found serial brain imaging unhelpful for prognosis, so this entry recommends ophthalmologic monitoring and does not recommend routine repeat neuroimaging. Indirect because it argues for the scope of surveillance by excluding a different modality rather than by assessing eye examination.

evidence.snippet: Close clinical and neurological assessment of these patients is mandatory to early detect and manage potential serious complications.
evidence.explanation: The longitudinal cohort explicitly recommends close assessment, without a defined interval.

treatments/3.description: Ophthalmologic assessment is relevant because optic nerve involvement can accompany canal narrowing, and progressive visual loss prompted transplantation in reported patients. The clinical series supports the indication but does not establish a surveillance interval.

evidence.snippet: The oral manifestations included anterior open bite, posterior crossbite, tooth eruption impairment, and hypoplastic amelogenesis imperfecta (AI).
evidence.explanation: The specific oral findings this care addresses - two malocclusion patterns, impaired eruption, and an enamel defect.

evidence.snippet: This study suggests that AI can be another feature of CAII deficiency syndrome.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own hedged statement that amelogenesis imperfecta belongs to this syndrome. Quoted as hedged because it rests on one patient.

treatments/4.description: Dental evaluation and appropriate restorative or orthodontic care address eruption disturbances, malocclusion and enamel defects. The clinical evidence characterizes the indication; it does not establish a tested CA2-specific dental treatment protocol.

evidence.snippet: Prenatal diagnosis requires mutational analysis of CA2.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that prenatal diagnosis is molecular.

evidence.snippet: In two opportunities for prenatal diagnosis, one from cultured amniocytes and one from chorionic villus biopsy, we demonstrated the general utility of the direct sequencing method for prenatal DNA diagnosis.
evidence.explanation: Documents prenatal diagnosis on both sample types.

evidence.snippet: The identification of the mutation in this family provided the opportunity for prenatal diagnosis in a subsequent pregnancy.
evidence.explanation: A worked instance of family-specific prenatal diagnosis.

treatments/5.description: Counseling can explain recessive inheritance and support informed reproductive choices. Familial CA2 variant testing enables carrier and prenatal diagnosis. Historical erythrocyte enzyme studies also detected reduced activity in obligate carriers.

evidence.snippet: A closed reduction and above-knee cast was applied after stabilization.
evidence.explanation: Directly reported orthopedic treatment in this patient.

treatments/6.description: Closed reduction with an above-knee cast was used after medical stabilization in the 2024 child with bilateral tibial fractures. The report describes subsequent healing; it does not establish a comparative orthopedic protocol.

evidence.snippet: He was started on potassium chloride (KCl) 30 mEq/L added to intravenous (IV) fluid.
evidence.explanation: Documents use in the individual report; no general efficacy estimate is inferred.

treatments/7.description: Potassium chloride was given for recurrent hypokalemia during the 2024 admission. This is correction of an electrolyte complication, not evidence of modifying the underlying CA2 disorder.

evidence.snippet: The patient was discharged on sodium bicarbonate therapy, lactulose and vitamin D3 supplements and has been followed up regularly.
evidence.explanation: Documents use in the individual report; no general efficacy estimate is inferred.

treatments/8.description: Vitamin D3 supplementation was included in the Jordanian child’s discharge treatment. The report does not establish a CA2-specific skeletal or neurological benefit.

evidence.snippet: Although this enzymopathy reveals how CA II is important for the skeleton and kidney tubule, the pathogenesis of the mental subnormality and cerebral calcification is less well understood.
evidence.explanation: The explicit statement that this arm is the unexplained one, contrasted with the two arms that are explained.

evidence.snippet: Correlation analysis revealed no significant associations between intracranial parenchymal calcium score and age, DQ score, or optic canal diameter.
evidence.explanation: The negative correlation that blocks the obvious inference from calcium burden to cognitive outcome.

evidence.snippet: Variability of brain calcification, cognitive disturbance and optic nerve involvement may imply additional genetic or epigenetic influences affecting the course of the disease.
evidence.explanation: Genotype-identical patients diverge on exactly the features in question, which is what makes this a mechanism gap rather than a sampling problem.

open_questions/0.rationale: Intracranial calcification and cognitive impairment are observed, but their causal relationship and their route from CA II deficiency remain unresolved. Calcification can be absent during childhood. In a ten-patient series, calcium score did not significantly associate with age, developmental quotient or optic canal diameter; this small negative study does not prove that calcium burden can never affect neurological outcome. The early transplant series suggested delayed calcification while developmental impairment persisted.

evidence.snippet: However, the prominent osteopetrosis found in humans with CA II deficiency could not be detected even in very old homozygous null mice.
evidence.explanation: The negative skeletal result in a confirmed protein null, which is the mismatch itself.

evidence.snippet: Like humans with the same inherited enzyme defect, animals homozygous for the new null allele are runted and have renal tubular acidosis.
evidence.explanation: The same animal reproduces the renal and growth arms, so the failure is specific to bone rather than a failed model overall.

open_questions/1.rationale: Car2-null mice reproduce growth restriction and renal tubular acidosis but did not develop osteopetrosis even at old ages. The reason for this species difference is unresolved. It limits translation of skeletal endpoints from this mouse, while leaving the model useful for renal physiology and for investigating compensation. The negative skeletal result should not be generalized to every cellular resorption assay.

evidence.snippet: Several mouse models of CA II deficiency have shown growth hormone deficiency, yet currently there is no standard pharmacologic therapy for patients.
evidence.explanation: Introduces the growth-hormone candidate, and in the same sentence records that no therapy is standardised.

evidence.snippet: Like humans with the same inherited enzyme defect, animals homozygous for the new null allele are runted and have renal tubular acidosis.
evidence.explanation: Growth restriction and acidosis co-occur in the null mouse, which is the observation behind the acidosis hypothesis - but it is co-occurrence, not a demonstrated mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Randomized administration of rGH from approximately 5 to approximately 12 wk to CAD mice improved food efficiency and increased serum IGF-I levels, final length, and weight compared with placebo without affecting blood pH.
evidence.explanation: Mouse intervention improves growth without correcting acidosis; it is not human treatment evidence.

evidence.snippet: Thus growth failure in CAD mice is associated with a decrease in GH secretion in males but not in females.
evidence.explanation: The endocrine observation is sex-specific in the animal study.

open_questions/2.rationale: Short stature is well documented clinically, but contributions from acidosis, skeletal disease and endocrine dysfunction remain unresolved. In CA II-deficient mice, low GH secretion was male-specific, and randomized GH administration increased linear growth despite persistent acidosis. This demonstrates a modifiable mouse growth phenotype, not an established human GH-deficiency mechanism or clinical treatment effect.

evidence.snippet: Following acetazolamide infusion, the CA II-deficient patients exhibited a prompt rise in urinary pH and HCO3- excretion similar to the response seen in control subjects.
evidence.explanation: The observation that creates the question.

evidence.snippet: These findings indicate that CA II-deficient patients, who lack detectable CA II in their erythrocytes, still expressed an acetazolamide-inhibitable CA activity in their kidneys.
evidence.explanation: The authors' inference that residual acetazolamide-sensitive activity persists in the CA II-deficient kidney.

open_questions/3.rationale: Patients with undetectable erythrocyte CA II nevertheless show a normal renal response to acetazolamide. The original authors set out three explanations - that the deficiency is not expressed in kidney, that another acetazolamide-sensitive soluble isoenzyme is expressed there in these patients, or that the response reflects the membrane-bound luminal carbonic anhydrase, a different gene product unaffected by the CA2 mutation - and favoured the third. This is recorded as an open question rather than settled because the entry's renal node depends on it: if luminal membrane-bound activity is intact, the human renal defect is a partial loss of tubular carbonic anhydrase function, not a total one, and the residual activity is a potential target. It also bears on the interpretation of acetazolamide challenge as a diagnostic test, which would be uninformative here.

evidence.snippet: In this kindred, two separate recessive disorders are penetrant, each affecting a different, tissue specific subunit of the vacuolar proton pump (H(+)-ATPase), providing a highly unusual, novel genetic explanation for the coexistence of osteopetrosis and dRTA.
evidence.explanation: The documented genetic phenocopy of the CA II deficiency phenotype.

open_questions/4.rationale: The clinical triad is a very strong pointer to CA2 and is often treated as diagnostic, but it is not pathognomonic, and the documented exception is instructive rather than merely pedantic. One kindred with osteopetrosis and distal renal tubular acidosis had normal CA II levels and no CA2 defect; instead two separate recessive disorders were segregating, a TCIRG1 deletion producing the osteopetrosis and an ATP6V1B1 mutation producing the distal RTA. Both genes encode subunits of the same proton pump, in tissue-specific isoforms. The practical consequence is that the triad justifies CA2 testing and the enzyme assay, but a negative CA2 result in a patient with the full phenotype should prompt a search for coinherited pump subunit defects rather than a presumption of a cryptic CA2 variant.

evidence.snippet: We observed significantly elevated basal calcium concentrations in bipolar patient platelets and lymphocytes compared to control subjects.
evidence.explanation: Direct measurement of the elevated basal calcium finding in 30 affective disorder patients versus 14 controls, the replicated peripheral-cell observation this node records.

evidence.snippet: our data suggest that storage operated calcium channels may be the source of the elevated intracellular calcium in platelets and lymphocytes of bipolar patients
evidence.explanation: Locates the abnormality at store-operated calcium entry rather than at the plasma-membrane voltage-gated channels implicated by the CACNA1C genetics, so the two calcium findings are complementary rather than the same lesion measured twice.

evidence.snippet: These results demonstrate that, in patients with BPD, abnormal Bcl-2 gene expression in the AA variant contributes to dysfunctional Ca(2+) homeostasis through a specific ER inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor-dependent mechanism.
evidence.explanation: Supplies a genotype-to-mechanism account for part of the calcium abnormality: reduced BCL2 expression in rs956572 AA carriers enhances IP3-receptor-dependent ER calcium release. Scope caveat -- 18 patient lymphoblast lines, a peripheral cell model, not neurons.

evidence.snippet: The aberrant behavior of AA cells was reversed by chronic lithium treatment and mimicked in variant GG by a Bcl-2 inhibitor.
evidence.explanation: Pharmacological convergence in both directions -- lithium normalizes the genotype-associated calcium phenotype and a BCL2 inhibitor reproduces it in non-risk cells -- which is what ties this node to the treatment section rather than leaving it as an isolated biomarker.

steps/0.description: Altered intracellular calcium handling is among the oldest and most replicated cellular findings in bipolar disorder: basal and stimulated cytosolic calcium are elevated in patient platelets and lymphocytes, and endoplasmic-reticulum calcium release through the IP3 receptor is enhanced in patient lymphoblasts carrying the low-expressing BCL2 rs956572 AA genotype. This is the cellular counterpart of the calcium-channel genetics curated under CACNA1C. Two scope limits are load-bearing and should not be read past: the replicated measurements are in peripheral blood cells rather than neurons, and they have not been shown to track mood state over time -- the original series found little correlation between calcium measures and mood-rating severity. The node therefore records a trait-associated calcium abnormality, not a demonstrated driver of episode switching (see the attached knowledge gap).

evidence.snippet: we have detected mitochondrial abnormalities in young neurons from patients with bipolar disorder by using mitochondrial assays; in addition, using both patch-clamp recording and somatic Ca(2+) imaging, we have observed hyperactive action-potential firing.
evidence.explanation: The primary measurement behind this node: patch-clamp and calcium imaging in patient-derived dentate-gyrus-like neurons show hyperactive action-potential firing alongside mitochondrial abnormalities, in patient-derived human tissue rather than an animal model.

evidence.snippet: This hyperexcitability phenotype of young neurons in bipolar disorder was selectively reversed by lithium treatment only in neurons derived from patients who also responded to lithium treatment.
evidence.explanation: The responder-selective rescue is what makes this node a candidate treatment-response stratifier rather than a generic cellular abnormality: the in-vitro correction tracks the donor's own clinical lithium response. It holds for the sampled lines and has not been shown to generalize across the heterogeneity of bipolar disorder.

steps/1.description: Patient-derived neurons show intrinsic hyperexcitability, offering a cellular endophenotype that sits between the ion-channel genetics and the circuit-level findings. iPSC-derived hippocampal dentate-gyrus-like granule neurons from bipolar patients fire action potentials hyperactively and carry mitochondrial abnormalities relative to control-derived neurons. The finding is also a treatment-response stratifier: lithium reverses the hyperexcitability only in neurons from donors who were themselves clinical lithium responders. Scope limits -- six manic bipolar I donors and four unaffected individuals, one differentiated neuron type, and no demonstration that hyperexcitability causes episode switching rather than marking trait vulnerability.

evidence.snippet: Psychiatric disorders (such as bipolar disorder, depression, and schizophrenia) affect the lives of millions of individuals worldwide.
evidence.explanation: This review discusses the molecular mechanisms underlying psychiatric disorders including bipolar disorder, with focus on the DISC1/GSK3 complex which regulates mitochondrial and cellular functions.

evidence.snippet: Strikingly, we found that the expression of multiple mitochondria genes was significantly enhanced in the BD neurons
evidence.explanation: RNA-seq of patient-derived dentate-gyrus-like neurons finds coordinated upregulation of mitochondrial genes, the first direct measurement supporting this node in patient-derived human neurons rather than by inference from review literature.

evidence.snippet: Flow cytometry analysis revealed that BD neurons showed increased red/green ratios, indicative of enhanced mitochondrial function
evidence.explanation: Note the direction: membrane-potential assay in young patient-derived neurons shows *enhanced* mitochondrial function, not the deficit the node description implies. Curated as a qualification -- the abnormality is established, but this study argues against reading it uniformly as impaired energy metabolism, consistent with the phasic model in which respiration is raised in mania and lowered in euthymia and depression.

steps/2.description: Impaired cellular energy metabolism and oxidative stress affect neuronal function. Mitochondrial abnormalities linked to mood dysregulation.

evidence.snippet: considering that schizophrenia is a multifactorial and highly polygenic disorder that shares many risk genes with other psychiatric illnesses including bipolar disorder, depression, intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorders, it is to be expected that these diseases may also share some of these same mechanisms
evidence.explanation: Microglial activation and inflammatory processes are shared pathophysiological mechanisms across psychiatric disorders including bipolar disorder, contributing to synaptic dysfunction.

steps/3.description: Elevated inflammatory markers during mood episodes. Microglial activation and cytokine abnormalities contribute to pathophysiology.

evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that lithium acts through inhibition of glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta (GSK-3 beta), which regulates cell fate determination in diverse organisms including Dictyostelium, Drosophila, and Xenopus.
evidence.explanation: Klein and Melton identified GSK-3β as a direct molecular target of lithium in developmental model organisms — the foundational evidence for the GSK-3β hypothesis of lithium's action in bipolar disorder.

evidence.snippet: Lithium potently inhibits GSK-3 beta activity (Ki = 2 mM), but is not a general inhibitor of other protein kinases.
evidence.explanation: Lithium inhibits GSK-3β at therapeutically relevant concentrations with selectivity over other protein kinases, supporting GSK-3β as a specific target.

evidence.snippet: Li+ treatment of Drosophila S2 cells and rat PC12 cells induces accumulation of cytoplasmic Armadillo/beta-catenin, demonstrating that Li+ can mimic Wingless signalling in intact cells, consistent with its inhibition of GSK-3.
evidence.explanation: In intact mammalian (PC12) and insect cells, lithium inhibition of GSK-3 stabilizes β-catenin and reproduces canonical Wnt (Wingless) signaling, tying GSK-3β inhibition to a defined downstream pathway.

steps/4.description: Glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK-3β) is a constitutively active serine/threonine kinase that phosphorylates β-catenin, tau, and numerous circadian and pro-apoptotic substrates. Excess GSK-3β activity is implicated in bipolar mood instability, and GSK-3β is the principal molecular target through which lithium is thought to exert its mood-stabilizing and neuroprotective effects. Lithium inhibits GSK-3β both directly (Mg2+-competitive) and indirectly (via the Akt / β-arrestin-2 / PP2A axis), stabilizing β-catenin and mimicking canonical Wnt signaling.

evidence.snippet: For more than 60 years, the mood stabilizer lithium has been used alone or in combination for the treatment of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, depression, and other mental illnesses.
evidence.explanation: This comprehensive review discusses lithium as the gold standard treatment for bipolar disorder, noting its mood-stabilizing effects through GSK3 inhibition which affects multiple cellular pathways including circadian regulation.

evidence.snippet: these data suggest that GSK3β acts as a critical intrinsic regulator of the circadian clock and plays an important role in regulating its period in response to lithium treatment
evidence.explanation: GSK3β haploinsufficiency lengthens circadian period in mice, mechanistically linking lithium's inhibition of GSK3β to its documented effects on circadian rhythm period and amplitude in bipolar disorder.

evidence.snippet: We found that knockdown of Clock, specifically in the VTA, results in hyperactivity and a reduction in anxiety-related behavior, which is similar to the phenotype of the ClockDelta19 mice.
evidence.explanation: Region-restricted RNA-interference knockdown shows that disrupting a single core clock gene in one brain region is sufficient to produce mania-like behavior, which is the strongest causal support available for the circadian pillar of this model.

evidence.snippet: However, VTA-specific knockdown also results in a substantial increase in depression-like behavior, creating an overall mixed manic state.
evidence.explanation: The qualification the model needs, quoted from the same result. The manipulation does not produce cycling between separable manic and depressive states; the authors characterize the outcome as a single mixed state. So this is a mouse demonstration that clock disruption destabilizes mood-related behavior, not a demonstration of the episodic switching the canonical model is invoked to explain.

steps/5.description: Disrupted sleep-wake cycles and circadian gene expression contribute to mood instability. Sleep deprivation can trigger mania.

evidence.snippet: Activation of the dopamine receptor 2 (D2R) has been shown to stimulate the inactivation of Akt by PP2A (Beaulieu et al., 2005; Beaulieu and Gainetdinov, 2011), therefore providing a mechanism through which GPCR activation can inhibit Akt in response to extracellular signals.
evidence.explanation: Dopamine D2 receptor signaling regulates the Akt/GSK3 pathway, providing a molecular link between monoaminergic neurotransmission and mood regulation in bipolar disorder.

evidence.snippet: This mechanism of D2R signaling appears to play important roles in the regulation of locomotor behavior and sensory motor gating by dopamine (Beaulieu et al., 2004; Emamian et al., 2004). It could also contribute to the therapeutic and/or adverse effects of psychoactive drugs like amphetamines and antpsychotics that act on dopamine neurotransmission
evidence.explanation: The D2 receptor-mediated regulation of GSK3 activity through beta-arrestin signaling is implicated in behavioral regulation relevant to bipolar disorder and the mechanism of mood stabilizers and antipsychotics.

steps/6.description: Imbalances in dopamine, norepinephrine, and serotonin neurotransmission contribute to mood episodes. Elevated dopamine in mania, reduced in depression.

evidence.snippet: DISC1 binds directly to GSK3 and modulates many cellular functions by negatively inhibiting GSK3 activity.
evidence.explanation: GSK3 inhibition by DISC1 and mood stabilizers like lithium is a key mechanism in bipolar disorder treatment, affecting synaptic plasticity and neuronal survival pathways.

evidence.snippet: In the present review, we will focus on the emerging roles of TRAX and its interacting proteins (including DISC1 and GSK3β) in psychiatric disorders and the potential implications for developing therapeutic interventions.
evidence.explanation: The TRAX/DISC1/GSK3β complex is implicated in psychiatric disorders including bipolar disorder and represents a therapeutic target for enhancing neuroplasticity.

evidence.snippet: Lithium's main mechanisms of action appear to stem from its ability to inhibit glycogen synthase kinase-3 activity and also to induce signaling mediated by brain-derived neurotrophic factor.
evidence.explanation: Lithium enhances neuroplasticity in part by inducing BDNF signaling and inhibiting GSK-3, directly complementing the reduced-BDNF pathophysiology captured in this node.

steps/7.description: Reduced BDNF and altered synaptic plasticity in mood circuits. Lithium and other mood stabilizers enhance neuroplasticity.

evidence.snippet: Inositol, however, reverses the effects of the drugs on growth cones, thus implicating inositol depletion in their action.
evidence.explanation: Williams et al. showed that lithium, valproate, and carbamazepine converge on inositol depletion — exogenous inositol rescues their shared cellular effect, direct evidence for the inositol-depletion mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Berridge and colleagues suggested that inositol depletion may be the way that lithium works in bipolar affective disorder, but others have suggested that glycogen synthase kinase (GSK3) may be the relevant target.
evidence.explanation: Frames the two leading molecular hypotheses of lithium action — inositol depletion versus GSK-3 inhibition — both of which are curated as distinct pathophysiology nodes in this entry.

evidence.snippet: By inhibiting the activity of phosphoinositol phosphatases, it decreases levels of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate, a process recently identified as a novel mechanism for inducing autophagy.
evidence.explanation: Lithium inhibition of inositol phosphatases lowers IP3 and links inositol depletion to autophagy induction, a downstream neuroprotective consequence.

steps/8.description: Overactivity of the phosphatidylinositol (PIP2 / IP3) second-messenger cycle is implicated in bipolar mood instability (the "inositol depletion hypothesis"). The cycle regenerates free myo-inositol through inositol monophosphatase (IMPase) and inositol polyphosphate 1-phosphatase; lithium uncompetitively inhibits these Mg2+-dependent phosphatases, depleting free inositol and dampening the overactive signaling — a therapeutic target shared with valproate and carbamazepine. (The disease-state direction shown here is the overactive baseline; lithium's opposing, inhibitory action is captured on the Lithium treatment's target_mechanisms edge.)

evidence.snippet: Levels of oxidative stress, pro-inflammatory cytokines and intracellular calcium ions are all higher in bipolar mania than in the euthymic and depressive phases of the illness.
evidence.explanation: States the calcium-to-mitochondrial-respiration step this edge encodes. Graded OTHER and INDIRECT because the source is an explanatory model paper synthesizing prior literature, not a study that tested the proposed sequence.

edges/0.description: Proposed rather than demonstrated. A published model argues that raised cytosolic calcium in mania drives increased mitochondrial respiration and ATP production, with the euthymic and depressive phases showing the opposite. No study cited here measures calcium and mitochondrial respiration in the same subjects across a mood transition, so the edge is recorded at unknown-intermediate directness.

evidence.snippet: VTA dopaminergic neurons expressing the Clock short hairpin RNA have increased activity compared with control neurons
evidence.explanation: The electrophysiological measurement that grounds this specific edge: clock-gene knockdown increases dopaminergic neuron firing, the step connecting the circadian node to the monoaminergic node.

edges/1.description: Clock-gene disruption raises dopaminergic output. Evidence is a targeted rodent perturbation; no human circadian variant has been shown to drive dopaminergic change in bipolar patients, so the edge is model-organism grounded rather than established in human disease.

evidence.snippet: We also found further support for the previously reported CACNA1C (alpha 1C subunit of the L-type voltage-gated calcium channel; combined P = 7.0 x 10(-8), rs1006737).
evidence.explanation: Landmark GWAS study providing genome-wide significant evidence that CACNA1C is a susceptibility locus for bipolar disorder, implicating calcium channel dysfunction in disease pathogenesis.

evidence.snippet: The finding for CACNG5, taken together with the earlier implication of CACNA1C and CACNA1B, strongly suggests a key role for voltage-dependent calcium channel genes in the susceptibility to bipolar disorder and/or schizophrenia.
evidence.explanation: Case-case GWAS analysis further confirms the critical role of calcium channel genes including CACNA1C in bipolar disorder susceptibility.

evidence.snippet: we performed electrophysiology and quantitative PCR experiments that demonstrated increased L-type VGCC current density as well as increased mRNA expression of CACNA1C in iNs homozygous for the risk genotype, compared with non-risk genotypes
evidence.explanation: Bridges the variant-to-function gap for the entry's flagship risk gene: induced human neurons from over 20 fibroblast lines show that the rs1006737 risk genotype raises CACNA1C transcript level and L-type calcium current density, fixing the direction of effect as gain of channel function. Scope caveat recorded by the authors themselves -- the rs1006737 haplotype is transdiagnostic and the donors included unaffected individuals, so this establishes a genotype-to-channel phenotype rather than a bipolar-specific circuit mechanism.

evidence.snippet: In the hippocampus, Cav1.2 inactivation enhanced presynaptic paired-pulse facilitation without altering postsynaptic LTP at CA3-CA1 synapses. In addition, CA1 pyramidal neurons of female CKO mice displayed a reduction in dendritic complexity and spine density.
evidence.explanation: Cell-type-restricted Cav1.2 loss in forebrain glutamatergic neurons produces behavioral, synaptic, and dendritic changes, establishing that the channel is functionally required in exactly the neuron class this model implicates. Graded INDIRECT because the direction is opposite to the human risk allele: this is a loss-of-function knockout, whereas PMID:25403839 associates the risk genotype with increased CACNA1C expression and current. The phenotypes are also not bipolar-specific, so the study is gene-function evidence rather than directionally convergent validation of the human risk edge.

genes/0.notes: Calcium channel

evidence.snippet: To identify susceptibility loci for bipolar disorder, we tested 1.8 million variants in 4,387 cases and 6,209 controls and identified a region of strong association (rs10994336, P = 9.1 x 10(-9)) in ANK3 (ankyrin G).
evidence.explanation: Genome-wide significant association of ANK3 with bipolar disorder in large-scale GWAS, establishing ankyrin G as a key susceptibility gene that may affect neuronal excitability and synaptic function.

evidence.snippet: In particular, we support prior findings in CACNA1C, and now identify ODZ4 as associated with BD.
evidence.explanation: Psychiatric GWAS Consortium large-scale GWAS established genome-wide-significant association of the teneurin gene ODZ4 (TENM4) with bipolar disorder.

evidence.snippet: Genetic variation in the neurocan gene (NCAN) showed genome-wide significant association with BD
evidence.explanation: GWAS with independent replication identified the extracellular-matrix glycoprotein gene NCAN (neurocan) as a genome-wide-significant bipolar disorder susceptibility locus.

evidence.snippet: was associated with a 1.8-fold relative risk for BD in our sample (P = 0.027; Fig. 1A).
evidence.explanation: The primary bipolar-disorder association, quoted with its effect size and p-value rather than from the abstract. The effect is nominal (P = 0.027, uncorrected), confined to a single founder population, and reported in a non-peer-reviewed preprint, so this is recorded as a lead rather than an established locus - see the linked knowledge gap for what replication would require.

evidence.snippet: homozygotes performing worse than heterozygotes, especially on the Verbal Memory subtest.
evidence.explanation: An allele-dose-dependent quantitative phenotype in adult carriers, which is a stronger genetic argument than the diagnostic association itself because it does not depend on case ascertainment.

evidence.snippet: Together, our observations indicate that LoF variants in SETD1A cause a range of neurodevelopmental disorders, including schizophrenia.
evidence.explanation: Peer-reviewed context for the gene, not for the bipolar association: SETD1A disruption already spans a range of neurodevelopmental diagnoses, which is the prior that makes a mood-disorder association plausible enough to record. It does not itself implicate SETD1A in bipolar disorder.

genes/4.notes: SETD1A encodes a histone H3K4 methyltransferase and is an established large-effect schizophrenia risk gene; its status as a bipolar-disorder risk gene is far weaker and rests, at present, on a single founder-population study. A missense allele enriched 55-fold in the Lancaster Old Order Amish (p.Pro596Leu, rs139187973) was associated with a 1.8-fold relative risk for bipolar disorder at nominal significance only (P = 0.027), in a non-peer-reviewed preprint. The allele-dose-dependent cognitive effect and the patient-derived iPSC phenotypes are the stronger part of that report; the diagnostic association itself is the weaker part, and is recorded here as a lead rather than an established locus. See the linked KNOWLEDGE_GAP discussion for what replication would require.

evidence.explanation: Table 1 row from the PGC bipolar disorder GWAS (41,917 cases): locus 9, index SNP rs2336147 at chr3:52,626,443 (GRCh37; 3p21.1), P = 3.6 x 10^-13, OR 1.070, named by the authors for ITIH1 and previously reported for schizophrenia and by the Cross-Disorder Group. This is the peer-reviewed genome-wide-significant bipolar association at the ITIH-cluster locus; the index SNP itself sits proximal to the ITIH genes rather than within them.

evidence.snippet: ConjFDR analysis revealed 2,143 pleiotropic SNPs jointly associated with BIP and OCD, with convergent signals at the ITIH3/ITIH4 locus.
evidence.explanation: Cross-trait conjunctional-FDR analysis of bipolar disorder and OCD GWAS summary statistics converges on the ITIH3/ITIH4 locus. PARTIAL because this is a non-peer-reviewed preprint and a summary-statistics analysis: it prioritizes ITIH3/ITIH4 among the genes at 3p21.1 but does not experimentally establish either gene as the effector.

genes/5.notes: ITIH3 lies in the extended 3p21.1 psychiatric risk region (GRCh38 chr3:52.79-52.81 Mb), immediately adjacent to ITIH1 and ITIH4 and within the same long-range LD block as GNL3, NEK4, GLT8D1, SFMBT1 and NISCH. Scope caveat: the index SNPs reported by the largest bipolar disorder GWAS are inside this region but not inside ITIH3 itself (rs2336147 is ~185 kb proximal to the ITIH cluster), so this entry records a locus-level susceptibility signal, not a demonstrated ITIH3 coding or regulatory effect. ITIH3/ITIH4 were specifically prioritized as the shared bipolar-disorder/OCD pleiotropic signal by a 2026 cross-trait conjFDR plus SMR/colocalization analysis, which remains a non-peer-reviewed preprint; the effector gene at 3p21.1 is still contested (see the attached knowledge gap). ITIH heavy chains covalently cross-link hyaluronan in the extracellular matrix, which would place this locus in the same ECM-remodelling theme as the established bipolar NCAN (neurocan) locus.

evidence.snippet: Combining gene-level results with SCHEMA, AKAP11 emerges as a definitive risk gene
evidence.explanation: Whole-exome sequencing of 13,933 bipolar cases and 14,422 controls establishes AKAP11 as a bipolar risk gene. The qualification is in the sentence itself: the definitive gene-level result requires combining BipEx with the schizophrenia SCHEMA analysis, so this is a cross-disorder rather than bipolar-specific finding.

evidence.snippet: At the protein level, AKAP-11 interacts with GSK3B, the hypothesized target of lithium, a primary treatment for BD.
evidence.explanation: The basis for reading AKAP11 as independent rare-variant convergence on the GSK-3 beta pillar of this model. Graded INDIRECT because the link is a protein-protein interaction reported by the same paper, not a demonstration that AKAP11 truncating variants change GSK3B activity in patients.

evidence.snippet: Genes implicated from genome-wide association studies (GWASs) of BD, however, are not significantly enriched for ultra-rare PTVs.
evidence.explanation: Records that the common-variant loci curated above (CACNA1C, ANK3, ODZ4, NCAN, the 3p21.1 region) are not the genes carrying the rare truncating burden, so the polygenic common-variant architecture and the rare-variant architecture are at least partly separate rather than two readouts of one gene set.

genes/6.notes: The one rare-variant risk gene curated for this entry, and the only one reaching exome-wide significance in bipolar disorder to date. Ultra-rare protein-truncating variants in AKAP11 are enriched in bipolar cases in the BipEx collaboration, but the headline gene-level result is reached only after meta-analysis with the schizophrenia SCHEMA exome data, so the risk is shared with schizophrenia rather than bipolar-specific. AKAP-11 is a PKA-anchoring scaffold that binds GSK3B, which is why the gene is read as rare-variant convergence on the pathway lithium is thought to act through; that inference rests on a protein-protein interaction, not on any demonstration that the truncating variants act via GSK3B or that GSK3B inhibition is lithium's necessary therapeutic mechanism. The same study found that common-variant GWAS loci are not enriched for ultra-rare truncating variants, so common and rare risk in bipolar disorder are at least partly distinct in their gene sets.

evidence.snippet: Lithium has been reported to reduce suicide rates and prevent manic episodes in individuals with bipolar disorder, major depression, or schizoaffective disorders
evidence.explanation: Lithium is the gold standard mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder with demonstrated efficacy in preventing manic episodes and reducing suicide risk through GSK3 inhibition.

evidence.snippet: In 1996, two independent studies (Klein and Melton, 1996; Stambolic et al., 1996) of the effects of lithium on cell signaling and development have identified a direct effect of lithium on the activity of GSK3 both in vitro and in cells.
evidence.explanation: Lithium's therapeutic mechanism involves direct inhibition of GSK3 and indirect effects through the Akt/beta-arrestin pathway, providing molecular basis for its mood-stabilizing effects.

evidence.snippet: By inhibiting N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor-mediated calcium influx, for instance, it suppresses the calcium-dependent activation of pro-apoptotic signaling pathways.
evidence.explanation: Beyond GSK-3β and inositol depletion, lithium contributes to neuronal calcium homeostasis by limiting NMDA-receptor calcium influx and downstream pro-apoptotic signaling.

evidence.snippet: We identified functional enrichment in focal adhesion and PI3K-Akt pathways, but we did not find an association with the ECM pathway.
evidence.explanation: Substantiates the pharmacogenomic qualification asserted in this entry's mechanistic-hypothesis notes. In 2,039 ConLiGen patients, the genetic signal for who responds to lithium falls in focal-adhesion and PI3K-Akt networks. Read precisely: the reported negative is for the ECM pathway, and the study did not test GSK3B or inositol pathways head to head, so it shows where the inter-individual response signal is rather than refuting the GSK-3β account of lithium's action.

evidence.snippet: The neuroprotective mechanisms involve inactivation of NMDA receptors through inhibition of NR2B tyrosine phosphorylation, activation of cell survival factors such as the PI 3-kinase/Akt signaling pathway, and induction of neurotrophic/neuroprotective proteins, including brain-derived neurotrophic factor, heat-shock protein (HSP), and Bcl-2.
evidence.explanation: Provides the reconciliation between the two previous items: PI3K-Akt is itself part of lithium's neuroprotective signaling, and Akt phosphorylates and inactivates GSK-3β, so a PI3K-Akt response signal is compatible with a GSK-3β endpoint rather than being an alternative to it. Graded INDIRECT because this is rat primary neuronal culture work reviewed in a neuroprotection context, and the cascade reconciliation was not tested in the ConLiGen response cohort.

treatments/0.description: First-line mood stabilizer, effective for mania and suicide prevention.

evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that lithium acts through inhibition of glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta (GSK-3 beta), which regulates cell fate determination in diverse organisms including Dictyostelium, Drosophila, and Xenopus.
evidence.explanation: Direct evidence that lithium acts by inhibiting GSK-3β.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Lithium inhibits GSK-3β both directly (Mg2+-competitive) and indirectly (via Akt / β-arrestin-2 / PP2A), stabilizing β-catenin and mimicking canonical Wnt signaling — the principal proposed molecular basis of its mood-stabilizing effect.

evidence.snippet: Inositol, however, reverses the effects of the drugs on growth cones, thus implicating inositol depletion in their action.
evidence.explanation: Inositol rescue implicates inositol depletion as a mechanism of lithium action.

treatments/0/targets/1.description: Lithium uncompetitively inhibits inositol monophosphatase and related phosphatases, depleting free inositol and dampening PIP2 / IP3 signaling.

treatments/0/targets/2.description: Through GSK-3β inhibition lithium lengthens circadian period and stabilizes clock-gene rhythm amplitude, addressing circadian instability in bipolar disorder.

evidence.snippet: Across modalities, lithium treatment was most consistently associated with larger volumes in the hippocampus, amygdala, anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), and prefrontal cortex (PFC), and with higher white-matter integrity within frontolimbic circuitry.
evidence.explanation: Locates lithium's structural association in exactly the fronto-limbic regions this model names, at the circuit level rather than the molecular level. Graded INDIRECT deliberately: a volume association is an inference step away from the plasticity mechanism this edge asserts.

evidence.snippet: Overall risk of bias was substantial, yielding low-to-moderate certainty of evidence.
evidence.explanation: The review's own certainty rating, curated alongside its headline result so the edge is not read as established causation. 78 of the 115 included studies were cross-sectional and only six were randomized, so the design base cannot separate a protective drug effect from confounding by who stays on lithium.

treatments/0/targets/3.description: Lithium induces BDNF signaling and upregulates neurotrophic/neuroprotective pathways, enhancing synaptic plasticity in fronto-limbic mood circuits.

evidence.snippet: Valproic acid is widely used to treat epilepsy and bipolar disorder
evidence.explanation: Establishes valproate as a mood stabilizer used in bipolar disorder and identifies histone deacetylase inhibition as a molecular mechanism of action.

treatments/1.description: Mood stabilizer, effective for mania.

treatments/2.description: Mood stabilizer, more effective for depression prevention.

treatments/3.description: Quetiapine, olanzapine, aripiprazole for mania and maintenance.

treatments/4.description: Used cautiously with mood stabilizer to prevent switch to mania.

evidence.snippet: participants assigned to IPSRT in the acute treatment phase survived longer without a new affective episode (P = .01), irrespective of maintenance treatment assignment
evidence.explanation: Randomized trial in 175 acutely ill bipolar I patients showing that acute phase IPSRT lengthened time to a new episode over two years of maintenance. Note the scope: patients entered acutely ill rather than euthymic, so this is not the prevention-from-euthymia trial the entry's chronotherapy gap refers to.

evidence.snippet: We observed no difference between the treatment strategies in time to stabilization.
evidence.explanation: Curated alongside the positive result to keep the claim bounded: IPSRT did not speed acute stabilization, and its benefit in this trial was confined to prophylaxis against later episodes.

evidence.snippet: the evolving pharmacological and psychological strategies in bipolar disorder is of utmost importance
evidence.explanation: This clinical review emphasizes psychological (psychotherapeutic) strategies alongside pharmacotherapy as core to bipolar disorder management.

treatments/5.description: CBT, interpersonal therapy, psychoeducation. Interpersonal and social rhythm therapy (IPSRT) is the arm that bears on this entry's circadian mechanism: it adds an explicit social-rhythm regulation component to interpersonal psychotherapy, and is the closest thing to a clinical test of whether stabilizing daily rhythms alters the course of bipolar disorder.

evidence.snippet: Ability to increase regularity of social rhythms during acute treatment was associated with reduced likelihood of recurrence during the maintenance phase (P = .05).
evidence.explanation: The specific result linking rhythm regularity to clinical course, and so the only clinical evidence in this entry bearing on the circadian node as a modifiable target. Graded INDIRECT because it is an association between an achieved process measure and outcome, not a randomized manipulation of circadian timing.

treatments/5/targets/0.description: IPSRT regularizes sleep and social routines, and greater achieved regularity during acute treatment tracks lower recurrence in maintenance. This is an association within a randomized trial rather than a demonstrated causal pathway: IPSRT is multicomponent, so the benefit cannot be attributed to the circadian component alone, and the social-rhythm analysis is mediational rather than a direct circadian perturbation.

evidence.snippet: The finding for CACNG5, taken together with the earlier implication of CACNA1C and CACNA1B, strongly suggests a key role for voltage-dependent calcium channel genes in the susceptibility to bipolar disorder and/or schizophrenia.
evidence.explanation: Existing canonical mechanism citation in the dismech knowledge base, used as the seed for the hypothesis-search deep-research run.

evidence.snippet: correlation analyses showed that BP subjects had similar, although less pronounced, gene expression alterations
evidence.explanation: Postmortem cortical transcriptome comparison finds BD subjects share schizophrenia-like gene-expression alterations, but only less pronounced ones concentrated among BD subjects with psychosis. The case-control study did not test the canonical calcium/circadian/synaptic model directly and did not restrict its BD sample to BD-I, so it qualifies rather than establishes that the model "best explains psychotic BD-I."

evidence.snippet: two BP patients failed to maintain improvement but responded again to nimodipine and remained well with a blind transition to another dihydropyridine L-type calcium channel blocker (CCB), isradipine
evidence.explanation: The decisive verapamil-to-dihydropyridine response switch cited for the pharmacological-subclass hypothesis involved only two bipolar patients within a 30-person mixed-diagnosis refractory-affective-illness cohort — a small case-series lead, not a demonstrated subclass effect.

evidence.snippet: concluding there is presently limited support for their efficacy
evidence.explanation: Review of calcium-channel-antagonist trials in bipolar disorder concludes that more recent, better-controlled studies found only limited support for efficacy, tempering the calcium-channel-blocker translational-failure claim.

evidence.snippet: TIMELESS and RORA genes may confer susceptibility to BD and impact on circadian
evidence.explanation: Single 2014 candidate-gene association study (353 SNPs across 21 circadian genes, meta-analysed across two internal BD cohorts) finds TIMELESS and RORA variants associated with BD. This is a circadian-gene lead from one study design, not a modern literature-wide meta-analytic replacement for CLOCK/BMAL1 priority.

evidence.snippet: these risk SNPs do not explain a large proportion of the structural brain alterations in BD
evidence.explanation: Candidate-SNP imaging study of CACNA1C, ANK3, ODZ4, and SYNE1 found no risk-variant-structural association surviving multiple-testing correction, refuting the premise that structural brain abnormalities are attributed to BD risk genes in the first place.

evidence.snippet: Brain structural abnormalities in major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and obsessive-compulsive disorder were highly correlated
evidence.explanation: ENIGMA mega-/meta-analysis finds shared cortical/subcortical abnormality patterns across BD, schizophrenia, major depressive disorder, and obsessive-compulsive disorder generally — a transdiagnostic pattern, not one specific to a psychosis spectrum or tied to BD-risk-gene status.

evidence.snippet: Isradipine or placebo (contains no active medication) will be used as an "add-on" to lithium, valproate, and/or atypical antipsychotics for individuals currently experiencing a major depressive episode.
evidence.explanation: A modern adjunctive-isradipine (dihydropyridine L-type CCB) trial for bipolar depression was registered, refuting a categorical "no modern dihydropyridine CCB trial" claim. ClinicalTrials.gov records it as Terminated for lack of enrollment (2 participants), so an adequately powered modern DHP-CCB trial remains a real gap rather than one never attempted.

evidence.snippet: We analysed data from participants of European, East Asian, African American and Latino ancestries (n = 158,036 cases with bipolar disorder, 2.8 million controls)
evidence.explanation: The 2025 multi-ancestry PGC4 GWAS (298 genome-wide-significant loci) is the current largest genetic-architecture study of BD, updating the polygenic-risk-locus evidence base beyond the smaller PGC3 scan the 2026 hypothesis-search report's genetics framing was based on.

evidence.snippet: Bipolar disorder risk alleles were enriched in genes in synaptic signaling pathways and brain-expressed genes, particularly those with high specificity of expression in neurons of the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus.
evidence.explanation: Genome-wide, hypothesis-free pathway enrichment is the strongest unbiased support for the synaptic pillar of this model: the risk alleles concentrate in synaptic-signaling genes expressed in prefrontal-cortex and hippocampal neurons rather than being spread across brain-expressed genes generally.

evidence.snippet: Significant signal enrichment was found in genes encoding targets of antipsychotics, calcium channel blockers, antiepileptics and anesthetics.
evidence.explanation: Drug-target enrichment ties the polygenic signal to the calcium and ion-channel pharmacology named by this model. Note the enrichment is shared with antipsychotic, antiepileptic and anesthetic targets, so it supports ion-channel involvement broadly rather than singling out L-type calcium channels.

hypotheses/0.description: Bipolar disorder is a highly heritable polygenic mood disorder in which common variants in CACNA1C, ANK3, ODZ4, and other ion-channel and synaptic genes combine with circadian/clock gene variants (CLOCK, BMAL1, NR1D1) to produce episodic mood instability. Mitochondrial dysfunction, calcium-signaling dysregulation, and altered neuroplasticity in fronto-limbic circuits (anterior cingulate, amygdala, ventral striatum) drive cycling between depressive and manic states. Lithium's mood-stabilizing efficacy (targeting GSK-3β / inositol monophosphatase / circadian amplitude), valproate's modulation of histone deacetylases, and the recurrent involvement of the dopaminergic reward system during manic episodes corroborate the polygenic-synaptic-circadian framework as the canonical model.

evidence.snippet: We also found little correlation between calcium measures and the severity of mood rating.
evidence.explanation: The null result that opens this gap. The same study that established the elevated-calcium finding found it did not track mood severity, so the field's most replicated cellular abnormality is not demonstrably state-coupled.

evidence.snippet: there is accumulating evidence indicating increased mitochondrial respiration and ATP production in bipolar mania which contrasts with decreased mitochondrial function in patients in the euthymic or depressive phase of the illness
evidence.explanation: States the phasic proposal that is currently the field's best answer to the switching question, and shows what it rests on: cross-sectional contrasts between mood states. Establishing that states differ is not the same as establishing what causes transition between them, which is why the gap remains open.

open_questions/0.rationale: Episodic cycling is the defining clinical feature of bipolar disorder and is the part of the canonical model with the weakest evidential support. Every pillar curated in this entry is a vulnerability or trait finding rather than a transition mechanism, and this shows up consistently in the primary sources rather than only in the abstract. The replicated peripheral-cell calcium abnormality showed little correlation with mood-rating severity in the series that established it (PMID:10418700), so the most reproducible cellular finding in the field is not obviously state-coupled. The patient-derived neuron work characterizes hyperexcitability as an early endophenotype in young neurons (PMID:26524527), not as a state marker. The strongest causal circadian manipulation available produces a single mixed state rather than alternation between separable poles (PMID:20591414). The phasic mitochondrial account that does address state (PMID:28093238) is explicitly a proposed explanatory model synthesizing cross-sectional comparisons, not a study of transition dynamics: comparing manic to euthymic subjects establishes that states differ, which is a different claim from establishing what moves a patient between them. This gap is the substantive content of the PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED verdict returned by the 2026 OpenScientist assessment of this hypothesis - the framework organizes vulnerability well and does not currently explain episodicity - and it is why the entry retains CANONICAL status for the vulnerability model without asserting a switching mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Among the novel pleiotropic genes, TPCN1, CACNA2D2, CACNA1D, and ATP2B1 are involved in voltage-dependent calcium channel activity, regulation of calcium influx, enriched in calcium-related pathway.
evidence.explanation: Genome-wide pairwise pleiotropy analysis identifies shared calcium-channel genes across psychiatric and cardiovascular disease, motivating the shared-axis question.

evidence.snippet: Our findings implicated that calcium-channel blockers and peripheral vasodilators elevated SCZ risk, diuretics reduced the risks of SCZ, BIP, and MDD.
evidence.explanation: Drug-target analysis underpinning the antagonistic-pleiotropy treatment-response gap for calcium-channel modulation.

open_questions/1.rationale: A genome-wide pairwise pleiotropy study in East Asians (Zhu et al., 2026; PMID:42436150) found shared genetic architecture across psychiatric and cardiovascular disease pairs converging on voltage-dependent calcium-channel activity, with novel pleiotropic genes (TPCN1, CACNA2D2, CACNA1D, ATP2B1) enriched in the calcium-signaling pathway alongside the established bipolar/schizophrenia locus CACNA1C. A calcium-pathway polygenic risk score was associated with prolonged QTc, and drug-target analysis implicated calcium-channel blockers and peripheral vasodilators in elevated schizophrenia risk while diuretics reduced risk across schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder. The unresolved gaps are (1) whether the same calcium-channel variants are the primary driver in brain versus a secondary consequence in cardiovascular tissue (tissue-specific direction of effect), (2) the causal direction of the calcium-genotype to QTc association, and (3) the mechanistic basis for the apparent antagonistic pleiotropy in treatment response - why L-type calcium-channel modulation may be relevant to mood episodes yet calcium-channel blockade associates with increased psychiatric risk at the population-genetic level. Resolving this bears directly on the safety of calcium-channel blockers in patients with concurrent bipolar disorder and cardiovascular disease. This is a cross-disease gap shared with the Schizophrenia, Major Depressive Disorder, and Coronary Artery Disease entries (dismech issue #6382).

evidence.snippet: was associated with a 1.8-fold relative risk for BD in our sample (P = 0.027; Fig. 1A).
evidence.explanation: The nominal, single-population association that motivates the gap.

evidence.snippet: associated with bipolar disorder risk and cognitive deficits in specific sub-domains.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own summary of what the variant is and is not shown to do - a risk association plus selective cognitive deficits, with no claim of an established bipolar-disorder locus.

open_questions/2.rationale: SETD1A is one of the most robustly established schizophrenia risk genes (genome-wide significant for rare loss-of-function variants in Singh et al. 2016, and one of ten exome-wide-significant genes in SCHEMA). Its relationship to bipolar disorder is not established. The only direct evidence is a founder-population missense allele associated with a 1.8-fold relative risk at P = 0.027 - nominal, uncorrected, single-population, and reported in a non-peer-reviewed preprint. Three things make this hard to resolve rather than merely under-powered. (1) The allele is 55-fold enriched in the Old Order Amish and rare elsewhere (0.09% in gnomAD), so direct replication in an unrelated cohort is not feasible for this variant; any replication has to be at gene level, on a different allelic series. (2) The schizophrenia association is driven by loss-of-function alleles, whereas P596L behaves as a hypomorph in patient-derived iPSCs, so a gene-level bipolar test is not testing the same perturbation. (3) Bipolar and schizophrenia diagnoses are not cleanly separable in carriers of large-effect chromatin-regulator variants, so a positive gene-level result would still need to distinguish a bipolar-specific effect from diagnostic assignment within a shared psychosis-spectrum liability. Until then the entry records the allele as a lead, not as a susceptibility locus comparable to CACNA1C or ANK3.

evidence.snippet: where multiple SNPs (e.g., rs3774364) colocalized with H3K27ac histone acetylation QTLs in the prefrontal cortex (PP_H4 > 0.5)
evidence.explanation: States the preprint's specific mechanistic proposal - prefrontal-cortex H3K27ac histone-acetylation QTL colocalization at the prioritized locus - which is one side of this gap.

evidence.snippet: Interestingly, differential expression analysis of GLT8D1, SFMBT1, and NEK4 suggested that rs2535629 may confer schizophrenia risk by regulating SFMBT1 expression.
evidence.explanation: The one functional dissection of a 3p21.1 psychiatric risk variant assigns the effect of an ITIH3-intronic SNP to distal genes, concluding SFMBT1 is the mediator. PARTIAL because the disorder studied was schizophrenia, not bipolar disorder or OCD; it constrains the gene assignment at this locus rather than settling it for these two disorders.

evidence.snippet: BD-OCD presents a more severe and complex clinical profile, requiring specialized assessment and integrated treatment approaches.
evidence.explanation: Peer-reviewed meta-analysis of 22 studies establishing that the bipolar-OCD comorbidity carries a distinct and more severe clinical profile, which is why a shared causal locus is worth resolving.

open_questions/3.rationale: 3p21.1 is genome-wide significant in the largest GWAS of both disorders, and a 2026 cross-trait analysis (conjFDR, SMR, multi-omic colocalization) prioritizes ITIH3/ITIH4 as the shared pleiotropic signal, with SNPs colocalizing with H3K27ac haQTLs in prefrontal cortex. That result is preprint-level, statistical, and directly contradicted in its gene assignment by the only functional dissection of the region published to date: CRISPR-Cas9 editing of rs2535629, which lies inside an ITIH3 intron, changed expression of the distal genes GLT8D1, SFMBT1 and NEK4 rather than of ITIH3, and the authors attributed schizophrenia risk to SFMBT1. So an intronic ITIH3 variant is a bona fide chromatin-regulatory variant at this locus while ITIH3 is not its target - which is precisely the confound a colocalization-only analysis cannot resolve. Resolving this matters because the two candidate effectors imply different biology: ITIH3/ITIH4 are hyaluronan-binding extracellular-matrix cross-linkers (the theme already represented by the bipolar NCAN locus), whereas SFMBT1 is a polycomb-family chromatin regulator of dendritic spine density. The clinical stake is real rather than hypothetical: OCD comorbidity in bipolar disorder is associated with a measurably worse course, so a shared causal mechanism would be a tractable target.

evidence.snippet: Our results show that Bcs1L transitions directly between the ATP and ADP conformations, with no indication of the existence of additional intermediate forms, supporting a concerted mechanism.

steps/1.description: BCS1L is an inner-mitochondrial-membrane AAA ATPase that delivers the folded Rieske iron-sulfur protein, UQCRFS1, during complex III maturation. Disease-associated genotypes impair this assembly function to varying degrees. A Bjornstad-associated p.Arg183His protein retained partial UQCRFS1 binding in a HeLa-cell co-immunoprecipitation assay. This supports impaired substrate engagement for that allele but does not directly measure insertion kinetics. Neither normal ATP turnover nor an identical substrate-binding lesion has been established for every Bjornstad genotype.

evidence.snippet: All mutant BCS1L proteins disrupted the assembly of complex III, reduced the activity of the mitochondrial electron-transport chain, and increased the production of reactive oxygen species.
evidence.explanation: The functional study reports assembly, respiratory and ROS abnormalities for the tested mutant set. Its cell-based biochemical findings should not be generalized to every subsequently reported allele.

steps/2.description: BCS1L dysfunction compromises maturation of Rieske-containing complex III and respiratory supercomplex organization. steps/4.description: The original functional study found increased cellular reactive oxygen species for its tested BCS1L mutants. Only the severe complex-III-deficiency mutant group also showed increased mitochondrial content in that comparison. These results support disturbed cellular redox metabolism but do not identify incompletely assembled complex III as the source of increased superoxide or establish a universal quantitative severity rule. Selective tissue injury is a further hypothesis.

evidence.snippet: Mutations that cause the Björnstad syndrome illustrate the exquisite sensitivity of ear and hair tissues to mitochondrial function, particularly to the production of reactive oxygen species.
evidence.explanation: This is the authors' mechanistic interpretation of the clinical and biochemical findings, not a direct tissue-specific oxidative-injury experiment.

steps/5.description: Oxidative injury is a proposed connection between disturbed mitochondrial function and the cochlear hearing phenotype. The reviewed studies do not directly demonstrate elevated ROS or hair-cell death in Bjornstad cochlear tissue. The annotated hair-cell types are candidate affected cells, not a reported histological finding. Relative vulnerability, energy supply and structural cochlear abnormalities require separate evaluation; a specific defect in potassium recycling is not established.

evidence.snippet: Additionally, the cortex in the samples showed loose keratin intermediate filaments (IF).

evidence.explanation: Places the lesion inside the follicle during keratinization rather than in the emerged shaft, which is what makes it a follicular rather than a cosmetic problem.

steps/6.description: Transmission electron microscopy in one Bjornstad patient showed wavy cuticle layers of variable thickness and loosely packed cortical keratin intermediate filaments. The authors localized the abnormalities below the infundibulum and proposed abnormal disulfide bonding; they did not directly measure a disulfide-bond defect or establish ROS as its cause. Ex vivo hair testing found reduced mechanical strength, consistent with the fragile, twisted shaft phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Bjornstad syndrome is a rare condition characterized by pili torti and sensorineural hearing loss associated with pathological variations in BCS1L.
evidence.explanation: The introduction identifies pili torti as a conventional defining feature; it does not estimate its population frequency.

evidence.snippet: The hair fibers of all the patients were twisted around their axis and devoid of any pigment.
evidence.explanation: Five affected members of one family, all with twisted hair fibers, documenting the phenotype within a single kindred.

steps/7.description: Flattened hair shafts twist around their long axis. Scalp hair is usually most affected, but other hair findings vary between reports. Pili torti is a defining sign in combination with hearing loss and is not specific to this syndrome alone.

evidence.snippet: In addition the patients had a moderate-to-severe degree of hearing impairment.
evidence.explanation: Documents the severity range of the hearing loss in all five affected members of one family.

evidence.snippet: Disease phenotypes are varied and can be as mild as Björnstad syndrome, characterized by pili torti and sensorineural hearing loss, or as severe as GRACILE syndrome, characterized by growth restriction, aminoaciduria, cholestasis, iron overload, lactic acidosis, and early death.
evidence.explanation: A review of all published BCS1L patients confirms sensorineural hearing loss as one of the two defining Bjornstad features.

evidence.snippet: with progressive sensori‐neural hearing loss noted from age 18 months onwards.

evidence.snippet: A retrospective report of two siblings with Bjornstad syndrome suffering profound SNHL unresponsive to conventional hearing aids treated with bilateral simultaneous cochlear implantation.

Aminoaciduria was neither confirmed nor excluded, leaving a potential additional contributor to hair loss.

evidence.snippet: Exposure to the neurotoxin occurs through ingestion of toxin (foodborne botulism), bacterial colonization of a wound (wound botulism) or the intestines (infant botulism and adult intestinal colonization botulism), and high-concentration cosmetic or therapeutic injections of toxin (iatrogenic botulism).
evidence.explanation: The clinical guideline distinguishes toxin exposure from colonization-mediated production.

steps/0.description: Preformed toxin is ingested, inhaled, or injected in intoxication forms, whereas wound and intestinal forms generate toxin after local bacterial colonization. These distinct routes converge on absorption into the vascular circulation.

evidence.snippet: Infant botulism is a severe neuroparalytic disease caused by ingestion of the spore-forming neurotoxic clostridia, including Clostridium botulinum that colonize the large intestine and subsequently produce botulinum neurotoxin in situ.
evidence.explanation: The review describes the upstream intestinal-colonization mechanism of infant botulism.

steps/1.description: In infant botulism, ingested spore-forming toxigenic clostridia colonize the large intestine and produce botulinum neurotoxin in situ before systemic distribution.

evidence.snippet: Botulinum neurotoxin enters the vascular circulation (through ingestion, absorption from colonized wound or intestine, inhalation, or injection) and is transported to peripheral cholinergic nerve terminals, including neuromuscular junctions, postganglionic parasympathetic nerve endings, and peripheral ganglia
evidence.explanation: The clinical guideline identifies vascular transport and the peripheral target sites.

steps/2.description: Absorbed toxin distributes to peripheral cholinergic sites, including skeletal neuromuscular junctions and postganglionic parasympathetic terminals. Direct central nervous system effects have not been documented in humans.

steps/3.description: The toxin heavy chain uses gangliosides together with serotype-dependent synaptic-vesicle protein receptors. BoNT/A binds SV2, while other serotypes use related receptor combinations; vesicle cycling exposes these receptors and enables receptor-mediated endocytosis.
