evidence.snippet: We observed lymphadenopathy (LAD), cytopenias, liver disease, cavum septum pellucidum (CSP), and increased CD4-CD8-B220-TCRαβ+ T cells (αβDNTs), in addition to the previously described features of an inverted CD4/CD8 ratio, CD4+ T lymphocytopenia, increased B cells, dysgammaglobulinemia, and decreased expression of the natural killer group 2, member D (NKG2D) receptor.
evidence.explanation: Enumerates the multisystem abnormalities in a 23-patient cohort.

steps/5.description: The wider phenotype attributable to hypoglycosylation of client glycoproteins beyond the immune compartment: lymphadenopathy, cytopenias, liver disease, cavum septum pellucidum, and — in patients ascertained by transferrin screening rather than by infection — intellectual and developmental disability as the dominant presentation.

evidence.snippet: MAGT1 has been described to be a subunit of the oligosaccharyltransferase (OST) complex and more specifically of the STT3B complex.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the molecular identity of MAGT1 as an OST/STT3B subunit, the basis for classifying this disorder as a CDG.

evidence.snippet: Transfection of MAGT1 mRNA enabled us to rescue proteins with defective glycosylation.
evidence.explanation: Rescue by MAGT1 mRNA establishes that the glycosylation defect is caused by MAGT1 loss rather than being incidental.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, MAGT1 deficiency is associated with an enhanced expression of TUSC3, the homolog protein of MAGT1, pointing toward a compensatory mechanism.
evidence.explanation: Documents TUSC3 upregulation as a candidate partial compensatory mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Although small, this study indicates magnesium supplementation is unlikely to be an effective therapeutic option in XMEN disease.
evidence.explanation: The trial's own conclusion, refuting magnesium supplementation as a therapy.

evidence.snippet: In vitro magnesium supplementation experiments in cells from 14 XMEN patients failed to significantly rescue NKG2D expression and the clinical trial was stopped.
evidence.explanation: Records both the in vitro failure and the fact that the trial was halted.

treatments/0.description:
Oral magnesium L-threonate and intravenous magnesium sulfate were tested on the now-superseded premise that MAGT1 deficiency is primarily a magnesium-homeostasis defect. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial (NCT02496676) found no change in EBV or NKG2D status, in vitro supplementation of cells from 14 patients failed to significantly rescue NKG2D expression, and the trial was stopped. One EBV-naive patient was withdrawn after asymptomatic elevation of liver enzymes on intravenous magnesium sulfate.
This entry exists to record a negative result, NOT to recommend a therapy. It is curated because the magnesium rationale is embedded in this disorder's name and in much of its older literature, so a curator or clinician meeting the entry needs to find the refutation here rather than infer efficacy from the historical framing.

evidence.snippet: Hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT), a standard treatment option for some PIDs, has a high mortality in XMEN patients due to post-transplant bleeding and is undertaken with extreme caution
evidence.explanation: Establishes HSCT as an option while stating the bleeding-related mortality that qualifies it; graded PARTIAL because the source supports availability but not efficacy.

treatments/1.description: HSCT is a standard option for some primary immunodeficiencies, but in XMEN it carries high mortality because of post-transplant bleeding and is undertaken with extreme caution. Recorded with that caveat attached rather than as a routine option — the thrombocytopenia present in 70% of patients is the reason.

evidence.snippet: Gene therapy is currently being pursued as an alternative to Mg2+ for treating XMEN disease.
evidence.explanation: Records gene therapy as the actively pursued alternative once magnesium was refuted; a statement of direction, not of efficacy.

treatments/2.description: With magnesium supplementation refuted, gene therapy is being pursued as the alternative disease-directed strategy for XMEN. Investigational only — no clinical efficacy result exists, and this must not be curated as an available therapy.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that the reduced steady-state levels of NKG2D are caused by hypoglycosylation of the protein and we pinpoint the exact site that is underglycosylated in MAGT1-deficient patients.
evidence.explanation: Directly demonstrates that the NKG2D deficit is a glycosylation defect, the central claim of this model.

evidence.snippet: We also performed glycoproteomics analysis on T lymphocytes and show that XMEN disease is a congenital disorder of glycosylation that affects a restricted subset of glycoproteins.
evidence.explanation: Glycoproteomic evidence reclassifying XMEN as a congenital disorder of glycosylation and noting that the affected glycoprotein set is restricted.

hypotheses/0.description: MAGT1 is a subunit of the STT3B oligosaccharyltransferase complex, so its loss impairs post-translational N-glycosylation of a restricted subset of client glycoproteins. On this model the immunological phenotype is a direct consequence of glycoprotein hypoglycosylation: the loss of steady-state NKG2D is caused by hypoglycosylation of NKG2D itself at a defined site, not by a downstream signalling defect. This is the model the current evidence supports.

evidence.snippet: These observations reveal a role for Mg(2+) as an intracellular second messenger coupling cell-surface receptor activation to intracellular effectors and identify MAGT1 as a possible target for novel therapeutics.
evidence.explanation: The originating report's own statement of the magnesium second-messenger model, including the therapeutic inference that motivated the later magnesium trial.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we challenge the possibility that supplementation with magnesium restores NKG2D levels and show that the addition of this ion does not significantly improve NKG2D steady-state expression nor does it rescue the hypoglycosylation defect in CRISPR-engineered human cell lines.
evidence.explanation: Direct experimental refutation of the magnesium-rescue prediction that defines this model.

evidence.snippet: No change in EBV or NKG2D status was observed.
evidence.explanation: Clinical refutation: the randomized controlled trial of magnesium supplementation found no effect on either endpoint.

hypotheses/1.description: The original model, in which MAGT1 acts as a magnesium transporter and the loss of NKG2D and of EBV cytotoxicity follows from a Mg2+ homeostasis defect, with supraphysiological magnesium predicted to rescue the defect. This model is retained here because it drove the disorder's original name, its clinical trial, and much of the older literature — but it is recorded as DEPRECATED. Magnesium did not significantly rescue NKG2D expression in CRISPR-engineered human cell lines or in patient cells, did not rescue the hypoglycosylation defect, and produced no change in EBV or NKG2D status in a randomized controlled trial.

open_questions/0.rationale: MAGT1-CDG is delineated as one disorder with two clinical presentations, both caused by defects in glycosylation. What partitions patients between them is unexplained. Candidate modifiers include which client glycoproteins are affected in a given genetic background, residual MAGT1 activity, the degree of TUSC3 compensation, and ascertainment bias — immunology clinics find EBV disease, metabolic clinics find abnormal transferrin. Until this is resolved, curators should not treat the two presentations as separate diseases, nor assume a genotype-phenotype correlation that has not been demonstrated.

open_questions/1.rationale: MAGT1 deficiency is accompanied by enhanced expression of its homolog TUSC3, which the source describes as pointing toward a compensatory mechanism. Whether that compensation is functionally meaningful — and whether it could be enhanced — has not been established, and the observation is currently an expression finding rather than a demonstrated rescue. With magnesium supplementation refuted, the therapeutic options for this disorder are limited enough that this is worth resolving.

evidence.snippet: Another hemizygous missense mutation, c.212G>A (p.R71H), was found in the same exon in two individuals (P2 and P3) of a German family
evidence.explanation: The second family's allele and its position in the same exon as the first.

evidence.snippet: Both mutations were absent from more than 60,000 control individuals in the ExAC server
evidence.explanation: The population-frequency argument, with its denominator.

evidence.snippet: A novel mutation, c.185G>A (p.Gly62Glu), was identified in exon 3 of ATP6AP2.
evidence.explanation: The third allele, in the same exon as the first two.

steps/1.description:
Three missense alleles are published across three families, and all three fall in exon 3, in the extracellular domain of the protein: c.293T>C p.Leu98Ser de novo in the Portuguese patient, c.212G>A p.Arg71His in two brothers of a German family, and c.185G>A p.Gly62Glu in the Chinese patient. Neither of the first two appears in more than 60,000 ExAC controls.
The clustering matters. The neurological ATP6AP2 diseases are caused by splicing variants that reduce the amount of normal protein; this entity is caused by missense substitutions in one domain that impair what the protein does. Allele class, not gene, is what decides which disease a patient gets — and even that separation is less clean than it looks, since the 2026 work finds glycosylation abnormalities in splicing patients too.

evidence.snippet: ATP6AP1 has recently been shown to be the orthologue of the yeast V-ATPase assembly factor Voa1
evidence.explanation: Why an interaction with ATP6AP1 is an interaction with the assembly machinery. Graded BACKGROUND because the paper is citing a prior finding in its introduction.

steps/2.description:
The V-ATPase is built in two sectors: the V0 proton pore, assembled in the endoplasmic reticulum under the control of a set of assembly factors, and the V1 ATP-hydrolysis domain, added in the Golgi. ATP6AP1 and ATP6AP2 are its two accessory subunits, and ATP6AP1 is the orthologue of the yeast V0 assembly factor Voa1.
So a variant that weakens the ATP6AP2-ATP6AP1 interaction is a variant that interferes with V0 assembly at its earliest step. That is the hinge of this disease: everything downstream follows from a pump that is not properly built, not from anything ATP6AP2 does on its own.

evidence.snippet: The multi-subunit vacuolar-type H+-ATPase (V-ATPase) acidifies intracellular organelles, thereby controlling several events in the secretory and endocytic pathway, such as proteolytic processing, protein degradation, autophagy, and glycosylation.
evidence.explanation: The pump's function and the four downstream processes this entry's branches correspond to. Graded BACKGROUND because it is established cell biology stated in the paper's opening.

evidence.snippet: We further demonstrate that in the liver-like fat body, the autophagic dysregulation was associated with defects in lysosomal acidification and mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling.
evidence.explanation: The acidification defect measured, in the Drosophila tissue that corresponds to the organ the human disease damages.

evidence.snippet: our data suggest that these phenotypes are the result of a pathogenetic cascade that includes impaired V-ATPase assembly, defective lysosomal acidification, reduced MTOR signaling and autophagic misregulation.
evidence.explanation: The whole cascade this entry's pathograph draws, stated in one sentence by the companion paper — and stated as what their data suggest rather than as established, which is the hedge the mechanism_confidence values here respect.

steps/3.description:
The V-ATPase acidifies organelles of the secretory and endocytic pathway, and through that controls proteolytic processing, protein degradation, autophagy and glycosylation. With V0 assembly impaired, those compartments are insufficiently acidified.
Defective lysosomal acidification was demonstrated directly in the Drosophila fat body — the fly's liver-like tissue — carrying one of the patient substitutions. That is where this node stops being an inference from the biochemistry and becomes a measurement, albeit in an invertebrate.

evidence.snippet: This missense mutation was found to dysregulate autophagy and mTOR signaling.
evidence.explanation: The third allele reproducing the same cellular phenotype as the first two, in an independent laboratory — which is what makes the autophagy branch a property of the disease rather than of one family.

evidence.snippet: metabolomics analysis revealed that the exogenously introduced Gly62Glu mutant resulted in the downregulation of numerous metabolites involved in lipid metabolism pathway
evidence.explanation: An untargeted metabolomic consequence pointing at lipid metabolism — the pathway whose disturbance the hepatic steatosis is the visible end of.

steps/4.description:
Autophagy is dysregulated and mTOR signalling reduced, shown in mouse liver, in the Drosophila fat body and in cells carrying the third patient's substitution. Patient liver shows what that looks like histologically: lipid accumulation and enlarged vacuolar structures within hepatocytes on electron microscopy.
This is the branch that carries the clinical disease. The liver failure, the steatosis and the cirrhosis track here, not through the transferrin profile — which is why the second founding paper is titled for autophagic liver disease rather than for a glycosylation disorder.

evidence.snippet: HPLC analysis confirmed that only half of the transferrin molecules (53.3% in patient 2 and 50.28% in P3) were present as the correctly glycosylated tetrasialo-transferrin
evidence.explanation: The quantified defect in two patients, which is what supports calling it partial rather than severe.

evidence.snippet: We show that ATP6AP2 deficiency in the mouse liver caused hypoglycosylation of serum proteins and autophagy defects.
evidence.explanation: That reducing ATP6AP2 in liver is sufficient to produce the serum glycosylation phenotype — the experiment that makes the link causal rather than correlative.

steps/5.description:
All patient sera show an abnormal transferrin profile — decreased tetrasialotransferrin with increased tri-, di- and monosialotransferrin — and HPLC put the correctly glycosylated fraction at about half in two patients. It is a type II pattern, meaning the defect is in processing rather than in assembly of the glycan.
The magnitude is worth stating because it is modest, and because it is the finding that gets this disease its name while not being the finding that makes patients ill. Half-normal transferrin glycosylation does not explain micronodular cirrhosis at sixteen months.

evidence.snippet: The 11-month-old Chinese boy presented with recurrent jaundice, cutis laxa, cirrhosis, growth retardation, coagulopathy, anemia, and cardiomegaly, and underwent liver transplantation.
evidence.explanation: The full presentation of the most severely affected patient, including the coagulopathy and anaemia this node names and the transplant that followed.

steps/6.description:
Coagulopathy and anaemia in the Chinese patient, ascites and portal collateral vascularisation in the Portuguese patient, and severe liver failure at five months in one of the German brothers. These are the consequences of losing hepatic function rather than separate processes.
Graded PROVISIONAL because the step from hepatocyte autophagic pathology to synthetic failure is the standard reading of liver disease and is not measured here — no synthetic-function study is tied to a cellular measurement in any of these patients.

evidence.snippet: ATP6AP1 deficiency manifests with hypogammaglobulinemia as well as liver and cognitive abnormalities
evidence.explanation: The sibling disease's phenotype, which is the only argument available that the antibody deficit belongs to the pump. Graded BACKGROUND and INDIRECT because it describes a different gene's patients, cited in this paper's introduction.

steps/7.description:
Low immunoglobulins with a poor polysaccharide antibody response, decreased CD4 and increased CD8 lymphocytes in the Portuguese patient; IgG subclass deficiency with reduced IgG1 and IgG3 in one German brother; normal immunological status in the other.
How a V-ATPase accessory subunit defect produces an antibody deficiency is not established in this disease at all. The most this entry can say is that hypogammaglobulinaemia is a recurring feature of the V-ATPase-related CDGs — ATP6AP1 deficiency manifests with hypogammaglobulinaemia alongside liver and cognitive abnormalities — so it appears to be a property of the pump rather than of this subunit. Hence HYPOTHETICAL.

evidence.snippet: Additional clinical features for all patients were cutis laxa (P1, P2, and P3), dysmorphic features (P1 and P2), mild intellectual disability (P1 and P2), and mild ataxia (P2; Table 1).
evidence.explanation: The four additional features with the patients each was seen in — the source for this phenotype's denominator and for the intellectual disability and ataxia entries below.

steps/8.description: Present in all three patients of the 2017 report and in the Chinese patient. It is the feature that, with hepatopathy and immunodeficiency, makes the clinical triad recognisable before sequencing.

evidence.snippet: led to a liver biopsy at 16 mo of age showing micronodular cirrhosis and steatosis
evidence.explanation: The histology and the age at which it was already established.

evidence.snippet: P3 developed severe liver failure at 5 mo of age. Liver biopsy revealed lipid accumulation and enlarged vacuolar structures within hepatocytes
evidence.explanation: The earliest and most severe hepatic course, with the ultrastructural correlate of the autophagic defect.

steps/9.description:
Micronodular cirrhosis with macro- and microvacuolar steatosis on liver biopsy at sixteen months in the Portuguese patient; lipid accumulation and enlarged vacuolar structures within hepatocytes on electron microscopy in one German brother; cirrhosis in the Chinese patient, who was transplanted at eleven months.
Cirrhosis before two years of age is the most consequential fact in this entry.

evidence.snippet: For P1, ascites, collateral vascularization, and hepatosplenomegaly and increased liver transaminases aspartate transaminase (AST) and alanine transaminase (ALT) led to a liver biopsy at 16 mo of age
evidence.explanation: The portal-hypertensive findings, and that they were what prompted the biopsy.

steps/10.description: Ascites with collateral vascularisation in the Portuguese patient — portal hypertension from the cirrhosis.

evidence.snippet: presented with recurrent jaundice, cutis laxa, cirrhosis, growth retardation, coagulopathy, anemia, and cardiomegaly
evidence.explanation: The presenting feature list in the fourth patient.

steps/11.description: Recurrent jaundice in the Chinese patient, who was transplanted at eleven months.

evidence.snippet: cirrhosis, growth retardation, coagulopathy, anemia, and cardiomegaly
evidence.explanation: The finding as listed for the fourth patient, alongside the cirrhosis that explains it.

steps/12.description: Coagulopathy in the Chinese patient, in the context of cirrhosis requiring transplantation.

evidence.snippet: coagulopathy, anemia, and cardiomegaly, and underwent liver transplantation
evidence.explanation: The finding and the outcome it accompanied.

steps/13.description: Anaemia in the Chinese patient.

evidence.snippet: recurrent jaundice, cutis laxa, cirrhosis, growth retardation, coagulopathy
evidence.explanation: The finding as listed. Graded INDIRECT because growth failure in a child with decompensated liver disease is not separable from the liver disease.

steps/14.description: Growth retardation in the Chinese patient.

evidence.snippet: Recurrent infections initiated immunological analysis that showed low levels of Igs, poor polysaccharide antibody response, decreased level of CD4+, and increased levels of CD8+ lymphocytes (Table 1).
evidence.explanation: The full immunological picture in the first patient, including the T-cell subset shift that the disease's name would not lead a reader to expect.

evidence.snippet: Similar to the other two patients, he has repeatedly suffered from infections, but his immunological status has so far been normal.
evidence.explanation: Graded REFUTE against treating hypogammaglobulinaemia as a constant of this disease. One of the three 2017 patients has recurrent infections with normal immunology — which also means a normal immune workup does not exclude the diagnosis.

steps/15.description:
Low immunoglobulins with a poor polysaccharide antibody response, decreased CD4 and increased CD8 in the Portuguese patient; IgG subclass deficiency with reduced IgG1 and IgG3 in one German brother. Both were given immunoglobulin replacement and both improved.
The second German brother has had repeated infections with a normal immunological status, which is the negative that keeps this from being a constant of the disease.

evidence.snippet: P2 suffered from recurrent pulmonary and upper respiratory tract infections throughout infancy and childhood.
evidence.explanation: The infection pattern in the patient described in most detail.

steps/16.description: Recurrent infections in all three 2017 patients: unspecified in the Portuguese patient, recurrent pulmonary and upper respiratory infections through infancy and childhood in one German brother, and repeated infections despite normal immunology in the other.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of protein N-glycosylation showed that all patient sera had abnormal transferrin glycosylation profiles with decreased tetrasialotransferrin and increased tri-, di-, and monosialotransferrin
evidence.explanation: The pattern, in every patient, with the isoform shifts that define its type.

steps/17.description: A type II pattern in all patients: decreased tetrasialotransferrin with increased tri-, di- and monosialotransferrin. It is the biochemical marker that assigns the entity to the CDGs, and it is partial — about half of transferrin is correctly glycosylated.

evidence.snippet: mild intellectual disability (P1 and P2), and mild ataxia (P2; Table 1)
evidence.explanation: The severity qualifier and the patients it applies to.

steps/18.description: Mild intellectual disability in two of the 2017 patients, and psychomotor impairment in the entity's description generally. It is mild, which is what distinguishes the CDG phenotype from the neurological ATP6AP2 diseases caused by splicing variants.

evidence.snippet: Finally, both ATP6AP2 mutations impaired protein stability and the interaction with ATP6AP1, a member of the V0 assembly complex.
evidence.explanation: The two measured molecular consequences of the first two alleles, and the partner whose loss of interaction connects them to V-ATPase assembly.

evidence.snippet: ATP6AP2 interacts with members of the V0 assembly complex, and its ER localization is crucial for V-ATPase activity.
evidence.explanation: The two facts this edge depends on — the interaction with the assembly complex, and that the interaction has to happen in the endoplasmic reticulum for the pump to work.

edges/3.description: ATP6AP2 interacts with members of the V0 assembly complex and its endoplasmic-reticulum localisation is required for V-ATPase activity, so an allele that weakens that interaction is an allele that impairs assembly of the pump.

edges/4.description: Golgi glycosyltransferases require an acidic lumen. A pump defect therefore produces a glycosylation defect without any glycosylation enzyme being mutated, which is what puts this entity among the CDGs of organelle homeostasis.

edges/9.description: Cutis laxa is present in all three of the 2017 patients and in the Chinese patient, and it recurs across the V-ATPase-related CDGs. Elastic-fibre assembly depends on secretory-pathway processing, which is what the pump defect disturbs, but no dermal or elastin measurement exists in any ATP6AP2 patient. The edge is the class argument, not a finding.

edges/10.description: Mild intellectual disability in two of the 2017 patients. The neurological ATP6AP2 diseases are much more severe and are caused by a different allele class, so the cognitive phenotype here cannot simply be read as a mild version of those — and the 2026 finding of shared glycosylation abnormalities complicates it further rather than settling it.

evidence.snippet: ATP6AP2 splicing variants cause syndromic X-linked intellectual disability Hedera type (XPDS; OMIM#300423) and X-linked parkinsonism with spasticity (MRXSH; OMIM#300911). Alternatively, ATP6AP2 missense variants lead to hepatopathy, immunological abnormalities, cutis laxa and only mild intellectual disability with N-/O-glycosylation defects (ATP6AP2-CDG; OMIM#301045).
evidence.explanation: The allelic series stated explicitly, with the OMIM identity of each entity — the basis for curating this as a separate disease from the neurological ones rather than as their liver variant.

evidence.snippet: RNA-Seq in patient-derived fibroblasts validated defective splicing, correlated with lowered ATP6AP2 protein levels in fibroblasts alongside glycosylation abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: The finding that connects the two entities — glycosylation abnormality in patients who have the neurological rather than the hepatic disease.

genes/0.notes:
The single causal gene, and one with two distinct diseases decided by allele class. Missense variants in the exon 3 extracellular domain give this entity: hepatopathy, immunodeficiency, cutis laxa, mild intellectual disability, glycosylation defects. Splicing variants give X-linked intellectual disability Hedera type and X-linked parkinsonism with spasticity: intellectual disability or developmental delay, epilepsy, axial hypotonia, axonal neuropathy and microcephaly, without hepatopathy.
The 2026 work makes that separation less clean rather than more. It finds defective splicing correlating with lowered ATP6AP2 protein and glycosylation abnormalities in four splicing-variant patients — so the neurological entity has the biochemical marker of the hepatic one. The authors call the disparity between the two an ongoing puzzle, and this entry does not resolve it.
ATP6AP2 is also known as the (pro)renin receptor. Nothing in this literature connects the renin-angiotensin function to either disease, and this entry does not import it.

evidence.snippet: IgG substitution was consequently initiated, under which the patient’s general health status improved.
evidence.explanation: The second reported response, in the German brother with IgG subclass deficiency.

treatments/0.description: Weekly subcutaneous immunoglobulin in the Portuguese patient, which decreased infection frequency; IgG substitution in one German brother, under which his general health improved. It treats the antibody deficit and does nothing for the liver.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Substitutes for antibody the patient does not make. It is recorded against the humoral phenotype because the pump defect that produces it is untouched.

evidence.snippet: coagulopathy, anemia, and cardiomegaly, and underwent liver transplantation
evidence.explanation: The intervention and the state it was performed in. No post-transplant outcome is reported in the abstract, which is why this treatment carries no outcome claim.

treatments/1.description:
Performed in the Chinese patient at eleven months for cirrhosis with coagulopathy and anaemia. No outcome beyond the fact of the transplant is reported.
Two things follow that a reader should weigh. A transplant replaces the organ but not the genotype, so the immunological, dermatological and cognitive features remain; and the serum glycosylation defect would be expected to correct, since the mouse experiment shows the liver is a sufficient source of it — which would make transferrin a useless marker of disease activity post-transplant. Neither point is addressed in any published source, and neither is asserted here as more than the reading it is.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Replaces the failed organ. The V-ATPase defect persists in every other tissue.

open_questions/0.rationale:
Until 2026 the separation looked clean and allele-based. Missense variants in exon 3 give hepatopathy, immunodeficiency, cutis laxa and mild intellectual disability with glycosylation defects; splicing variants give X-linked intellectual disability Hedera type or X-linked parkinsonism with spasticity, with no liver disease. The 2017 paper reinforced it by showing that a patient with a known exon-skipping variant had a normal transferrin profile.
The 2026 study looked harder and found glycosylation abnormalities in four splicing-variant patients, alongside reduced ATP6AP2 protein — and concluded that abnormal glycosylation may be a consistent feature of the splicing variants and potentially part of their pathological mechanism. Its own authors call the disparity between the neurological and hepatic entities an ongoing puzzle.
Three readings are live. One gene, two diseases, with the glycosylation finding incidental. One disease with a modifier that determines organ involvement. Or a dosage-versus-function distinction: splicing variants reduce how much protein there is, missense variants in one domain break what it does, and those are different lesions that happen to share a marker.
dismech keeps them separate for now, with this entry naming the neurological entities and their OMIM identities so that a curator arriving from the other direction finds the link. What would settle it is liver assessment in splicing patients and neurological assessment in missense patients, neither of which has been done systematically.

open_questions/1.rationale:
The entity is named for its glycosylation and classified among the CDGs, and the glycosylation abnormality is what put its first patients in the cohort they were found in. But it is modest — about half of transferrin is correctly glycosylated — and it is hard to see half-normal transferrin sialylation producing micronodular cirrhosis at sixteen months.
The autophagy branch looks more proportionate to the clinical disease: impaired lysosomal acidification, dysregulated autophagy, reduced mTOR signalling, lipid accumulation and enlarged vacuolar structures in hepatocytes, and downregulated lipid-metabolism metabolites. The second founding paper is titled for autophagic liver disease rather than for a glycosylation disorder, which suggests its authors saw the same thing.
This entry draws both branches from the acidification node and does not rank them. The question matters practically: if glycosylation is a biomarker rather than a cause, then a normal transferrin profile should not reassure, and improvement in transferrin should not be read as improvement in disease.

open_questions/2.rationale:
Two of four patients have an antibody deficiency, one with a poor polysaccharide response and a decreased CD4 with increased CD8 count. Nothing in this literature measures anything immunological below the level of the serum immunoglobulin and the flow count — no B-cell subset work, no class-switching, no plasma-cell study, and no measurement of organelle pH in a lymphocyte.
The only argument available is by family resemblance: ATP6AP1 deficiency, the sibling V-ATPase CDG, also manifests with hypogammaglobulinaemia. That makes it look like a property of the pump. It is not a mechanism, and the node in this entry is graded HYPOTHETICAL accordingly.
The negative in the same series is what makes the gap interesting rather than merely unfilled: the third 2017 patient has recurrent infections with a normal immunological status. Whatever the mechanism is, it is not obligate.

evidence.snippet: Animal studies implicate maternal diabetes and prenatal exposure to ethanol, retinoids, theophylline, and valproate in DORV teratogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Names maternal diabetes among the exposures implicated in DORV teratogenesis; the supporting studies cited are animal studies, hence MODEL_ORGANISM.

evidence.snippet: Animal studies implicate maternal diabetes and prenatal exposure to ethanol, retinoids, theophylline, and valproate in DORV teratogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Directly names the teratogenic exposures implicated in DORV in animal studies.

evidence.snippet: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and double-outlet right ventricle (DORV) are conotruncal defects resulting from disturbances of the second heart field and the neural crest, which can occur as isolated malformations or as part of multiorgan syndromes.
evidence.explanation: Directly identifies disturbance of the second heart field and the neural crest as the developmental origin of DORV.

evidence.snippet: The large number of genes associated with DORV in both humans and animal models and the different anatomic subtypes seen in specific aetiologies indicate the likelihood of several distinct pathogenetic mechanisms for DORV, including impairment of neural crest derivative migration and impairment of normal cardiac situs and looping.
evidence.explanation: Supports impaired neural crest derivative migration as one of the distinct pathogenetic mechanisms of DORV, alongside disturbed situs and looping.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrate Shroom3 expression within cardiomyocytes of the ventricles and interventricular septum from E10.5 onward, as well as within cardiac neural crest cells and second heart field cells that populate the cardiac outflow tract.
evidence.explanation: Localises a DORV-causing planar-cell-polarity effector to precisely the cardiac neural crest and second-heart-field populations that build the outflow tract.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that Shroom3gt/gt mice exhibit variable penetrance of a spectrum of CHDs that include ventricular septal defects, double outlet right ventricle, and thin left ventricular myocardium.
evidence.explanation: Shows experimentally that disrupting a planar-cell-polarity effector in these progenitor populations produces DORV.

steps/2.description: DORV originates in the two extracardiac progenitor populations that build the cardiac outflow tract. Cardiac neural crest cells delaminate from the dorsal neural tube, migrate through the caudal pharyngeal arches into the distal outflow tract and condense to form the aorticopulmonary septum, while second-heart-field progenitors are added to the arterial pole and provide the myocardium that elongates and rotates the outflow tract. Genetic lesions (chromosomal, transcription-factor, planar-cell-polarity, ciliary) and teratogenic exposures that perturb neural crest migration or second-heart-field addition converge on this step. DORV and tetralogy of Fallot are the two conotruncal phenotypes that most directly report this disturbance.

evidence.snippet: Since Van Praagh type III DORV is associated with heterotaxy
evidence.explanation: Establishes the heterotaxy-associated (laterality) aetiologic class of DORV; PARTIAL because the source goes on to frame the specific laterality genes as predicted candidates rather than established causes.

evidence.snippet: Complex CHDs revealed by histological analysis include atrioventricular septal defects, DORV, single ventricle defects as well as abnormal position of the great arteries.
evidence.explanation: Loss of the master motile-cilia transcription factor Foxj1 in mice produces DORV together with abnormal great-artery position, tying ciliary laterality failure to the double-outlet connection.

evidence.snippet: Finally, we characterize embryonic-stage CHD in Foxj1 loss-of-function mice, demonstrating randomized heart looping.
evidence.explanation: Directly links disrupted ciliary left-right patterning to randomised cardiac looping, the morphogenetic step that misaligns the arterial poles.

evidence.snippet: The large number of genes associated with DORV in both humans and animal models and the different anatomic subtypes seen in specific aetiologies indicate the likelihood of several distinct pathogenetic mechanisms for DORV, including impairment of neural crest derivative migration and impairment of normal cardiac situs and looping.
evidence.explanation: Names impairment of normal cardiac situs and looping as a pathogenetic mechanism of DORV distinct from the neural crest route.

steps/3.description: A distinct upstream route to DORV runs through the left-right organiser. Motile monocilia at the embryonic node generate leftward flow that establishes the NODAL laterality cascade; failure of this step randomises cardiac looping and the spatial relationship of the great arteries. This is the mechanism behind Van Praagh type III DORV, the form associated with heterotaxy and atrial isomerism, and explains why laterality genes (ZIC3, CFC1, FOXJ1, NODAL-pathway genes) recur in DORV cohorts. Because a randomised or abnormal loop misplaces the ventricles relative to the arterial poles, it produces the same double-outlet connection by a different developmental route than a primary neural-crest defect.

evidence.snippet: We postulate that normally the pulmonary trunk and orifice are pushed in a higher and more frontal position relative to the aortic orifice by asymmetric addition of SHF-myocardium.
evidence.explanation: Describes the second-heart-field-driven rotation mechanism whose failure is proposed here as the alignment defect underlying DORV.

evidence.snippet: Deficient or disorganized right ventricular OFT expansion might explain cardiac malformations with abnormal position of the great arteries, such as double outlet right ventricle.
evidence.explanation: Proposes deficient outflow tract expansion and rotation as the explanation for DORV; PARTIAL because the source frames it as a postulate.

evidence.snippet: DORV is not a disease entity in itself, but rather a vast spectrum of disorders associated with maldevelopment of conal muscle and often abnormal expansion of one the great vessels.
evidence.explanation: Frames DORV as the consequence of conal maldevelopment and abnormal great-vessel expansion rather than a discrete entity.

steps/4.description: Normally the arterial pole rotates during looping so the aorta swings rightward and posteriorly over the left ventricle while the pulmonary trunk is displaced anteriorly and leftward. This rotation is driven in part by asymmetric addition of second-heart-field myocardium at the pulmonary side of the outflow tract, which pushes the pulmonary orifice into a higher, more frontal position relative to the aortic orifice (the "pulmonary push"). Deficient or disorganised right ventricular outflow tract expansion leaves the rotation incomplete, so the aortic root is never transferred across the ventricular septum and remains supported by the right ventricle.

evidence.snippet: Normally, the subaortic conus resorbs and brings the aorta in continuity with the mitral valve
evidence.explanation: States the normal developmental event, resorption of the subaortic conus producing aorto-mitral continuity, whose failure defines this node.

evidence.snippet: In DORV, the subaortic conus frequently persists
evidence.explanation: Directly documents persistence of the subaortic conus as the characteristic conal abnormality of DORV.

evidence.snippet: In this review, we aim to underscore the importance of conal muscle, rather than rules surrounding assignment of great arteries to ventricles.
evidence.explanation: Supports conal muscle, rather than the arbitrary 50% override rule, as the substantive anatomic determinant in DORV.

evidence.snippet: It was considered, for many years, that presence of bilateral infundibulums, or conuses, was a necessity for such a diagnosis.
evidence.explanation: Records the historical bilateral-conus criterion while flagging that it is no longer regarded as necessary, which is why this node is described as characteristic rather than obligatory.

evidence.snippet: The latter condition is the more common type of DORV
evidence.explanation: Refutes any obligatory reading of this node: the form of DORV with atrioventricular-to-arterial valvar fibrous continuity, i.e. without a complete bilateral conus, is stated to be the more common type. Persistence of the subaortic conus is therefore a characteristic but not a necessary feature.

steps/5.description: In the normal heart the subpulmonary conus persists while the subaortic conal free wall resorbs, allowing the aortic valve to descend into fibrous continuity with the mitral valve. In DORV the subaortic conus characteristically persists, producing bilateral (subaortic and subpulmonary) infundibula and abolishing aorto-mitral fibrous continuity, so the aortic root remains elevated on a muscular sleeve above the right ventricle. This is the conal basis of the classical "50% rule": what is really being measured is whether conal muscle still interposes between the arterial root and the left ventricle. The criterion is not absolute, because DORV also occurs with fibrous continuity between the arterial and atrioventricular valves, so bilateral conus is sufficient but not necessary for the diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: DORV was defined as a congenital cardiovascular malformation in which both great arteries arise entirely or predominantly from the morphologically right ventricle.
evidence.explanation: Gives the current consensus (ICD-11) definition of the double-outlet ventriculo-arterial connection modelled by this node.

evidence.snippet: Each great artery should have 50% or greater of the valve diameter coming from the morphologic RV, and there is almost always an interventricular communication: ventricular septal defect (VSD) or atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD)
evidence.explanation: Supports both the double-outlet criterion and the near-obligatory presence of an interventricular communication as the sole left ventricular outlet.

evidence.snippet: In rare cases, where the interventricular communication is restricted or absent
evidence.explanation: Documents the rare variant in which no adequate interventricular communication exists, the situation that drives left ventricular hypoplasia.

steps/6.description: The defining lesion: both arterial trunks arise entirely or predominantly from the morphologic right ventricle. Because the left ventricle has lost its direct arterial outlet, an interventricular communication is obligatory for viable left ventricular egress; a ventricular septal defect (or, in the setting of an atrioventricular septal defect, the common interventricular communication) is therefore present in almost every case. When the interventricular communication is restrictive or absent, the left ventricle receives no adequate outlet and becomes hypoplastic.

evidence.snippet: when both arterial trunks arise exclusively or predominantly from the morphologically right ventricle, the outlet septum, of necessity, is itself a right ventricular structure
evidence.explanation: Establishes the anatomic premise that makes outlet-septum attachment the determinant of VSD commitment in DORV.

evidence.snippet: it is the attachment of the outlet septum, which itself can be muscular or fibrous, which determines the commitment of the interventricular communication to the subarterial outlets
evidence.explanation: Directly states the causal relationship modelled by this node.

evidence.snippet: The location of the VSD in DORV as viewed from the morphologic RV may be subpulmonic, subaortic, doubly committed
evidence.explanation: Enumerates the positional categories of the interventricular communication that this node generates.

evidence.snippet: This anatomic variability directly determines physiology and surgical repair options.
evidence.explanation: Supports the central claim that the anatomic variant, not the DORV label, drives physiology and repair choice.

steps/7.description: Because both arterial trunks are supported by the right ventricle, the outlet septum is itself a right ventricular structure, and the channel between the ventricles is roofed by the inner heart curvature. It is therefore the attachment of the outlet septum, muscular or fibrous, that determines to which subarterial outlet the interventricular communication is committed: the cranial limb of the septomarginal trabeculation gives a subaortic defect, the caudal limb a subpulmonary defect, and the inner heart curvature a doubly committed defect, while defects lying outside the limbs of the trabeculation are non-committed. This single anatomic variable, rather than the DORV label, determines the streaming physiology and the repair strategy.

evidence.snippet: The displacement of this outlet septum into the aortic or pulmonary out
evidence.explanation: Identifies displacement of the muscular outlet septum into either outflow tract as the mechanism generating subvalvar obstruction in DORV.

evidence.snippet: A subaortic VSD may mean that pulmonary stenosis and small branch pulmonary arteries are likely to develop.
evidence.explanation: Links the subaortic VSD variant specifically to the development of pulmonary stenosis.

evidence.snippet: A wide variety of cardiac malformations of the heart may accompany DORV including coarctation of the aorta (CoA)
evidence.explanation: Documents aortic coarctation among the associated left-sided obstructive lesions of DORV.

evidence.snippet: Hypoplastic ventricles were present in 39%, pulmonary stenosis was present in 65%, and aortic arch obstruction was present in 24%.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the frequency of pulmonary stenosis and aortic arch obstruction generated by outlet septum malalignment in a large DORV cohort.

steps/8.description: The muscular outlet septum partitions the two infundibula, and its displacement into either outflow tract creates subvalvar obstruction. Deviation into the subpulmonary outflow produces subpulmonary and pulmonary stenosis, the lesion that gives a subaortic-VSD heart its Fallot-type physiology. Deviation into the subaortic outflow, or a subpulmonary VSD that diverts fetal left ventricular flow away from the systemic outlet, produces subaortic stenosis and is associated with hypoplasia of the aortic arch, coarctation and interrupted aortic arch, the lesions that dominate the Taussig-Bing anomaly. Chronic obstruction to right ventricular ejection also drives right ventricular hypertrophy.

evidence.snippet: the LV will show an element of hypoplasia, which can vary from mild to severe
evidence.explanation: Documents left ventricular hypoplasia as the consequence of a restricted or absent interventricular communication in DORV.

evidence.snippet: Contraindications to biventricular repair include severe ventricular hypoplasia, abnormal tricuspid chordae, multiple VSDs, and a straddling mitral valve.
evidence.explanation: Establishes ventricular hypoplasia and associated valve anomalies as the determinants that preclude biventricular repair.

evidence.snippet: Factors discriminating among end-states included younger patient age at presentation (P < .001), lower weight (P < .001), and adequacy of left-sided heart structures, especially the size of the left ventricle (P < .001), aortic arch (P < .001), and mitral valve (P = .004).
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates empirically that the adequacy of left-sided structures, especially left ventricular size, determines which definitive end-state a DORV patient reaches.

steps/9.description: When the interventricular communication is restrictive, remote from both arterial roots, or absent, fetal left ventricular filling and ejection are reduced and the left ventricle fails to grow. The same anatomic circumstances that limit left ventricular growth, together with straddling or hypoplastic atrioventricular valves and multiple ventricular septal defects, also make an unobstructed intraventricular baffle impossible. This node is therefore the hinge on which the entire management pathway turns: it converts DORV from a biventricular repair problem into a single-ventricle palliation problem.

evidence.snippet: This anatomic variability directly determines physiology and surgical repair options.
evidence.explanation: Supports the dependence of DORV physiology on the underlying anatomic variant, the core claim of this node.

evidence.snippet: patients with subaortic VSD or subpulmonary VSD can have pulmonary over-circulation requiring aggressive diuresis
evidence.explanation: Documents pulmonary overcirculation as a direct physiologic consequence of unobstructed VSD-mediated shunting in DORV.

evidence.snippet: These patients may develop increasing cyanosis over time and may even develop hyper-cyanotic spells like patients with TOF.
evidence.explanation: Supports progressive cyanosis, including hypercyanotic spells, as the alternative physiologic expression when pulmonary blood flow is restricted.

steps/10.description: All left ventricular output must traverse the ventricular septal defect into the right ventricle, so systemic and pulmonary venous returns mix obligatorily. The clinical expression depends on where the defect sits. With a subaortic defect, oxygenated left ventricular blood streams preferentially into the adjacent aorta and desaturated right ventricular blood into the pulmonary artery, giving a large-VSD physiology with only mild desaturation but marked pulmonary overcirculation. With a subpulmonary (Taussig-Bing) defect the streaming is reversed: oxygenated blood is directed into the pulmonary artery while desaturated systemic venous blood is ejected into the aorta, producing transposition-like physiology with early profound cyanosis. Any superimposed pulmonary stenosis restricts pulmonary blood flow and shifts even a subaortic defect toward cyanosis.

evidence.snippet: patients with subaortic VSD or subpulmonary VSD can have pulmonary over-circulation requiring aggressive diuresis
evidence.explanation: Documents pulmonary overcirculation and the need for decongestive therapy as a direct consequence of unrestricted shunting in DORV.

evidence.snippet: At times, this may lead to the need for respiratory support and intubation.
evidence.explanation: Supports the respiratory consequences of pulmonary overcirculation in DORV infants.

steps/11.description: In the absence of pulmonary stenosis, the postnatal fall in pulmonary vascular resistance allows a torrential left-to-right shunt through the ventricular septal defect and into the pulmonary artery. The resulting pulmonary overcirculation produces tachypnoea, feeding difficulty and failure to thrive within the first weeks of life, ventricular volume overload and congestive heart failure, and, if repair is delayed beyond infancy, progressive pulmonary vascular remodelling and irreversible pulmonary arterial hypertension. This is the rationale for completing biventricular repair within the first six months of life or, when repair must be deferred, for interim pulmonary artery banding.

evidence.snippet: DORV was defined as a congenital cardiovascular malformation in which both great arteries arise entirely or predominantly from the morphologically right ventricle.
evidence.explanation: States the defining anatomic criterion, which is the phenotype itself.

steps/12.description: The defining anatomic lesion: both great arteries arise entirely or predominantly from the morphologic right ventricle, with a ventricular septal defect as the only left ventricular outlet.

evidence.snippet: Each great artery should have 50% or greater of the valve diameter coming from the morphologic RV, and there is almost always an interventricular communication: ventricular septal defect (VSD) or atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD)
evidence.explanation: Documents the near-universal presence of an interventricular communication in DORV and supports the VERY_FREQUENT frequency band.

steps/13.description: An interventricular communication is present in almost every case of DORV and is the sole outlet from the left ventricle. Its position relative to the arterial roots defines the anatomic subtypes.

evidence.snippet: These patients may develop increasing cyanosis over time and may even develop hyper-cyanotic spells like patients with TOF.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents progressive cyanosis and hypercyanotic spells as clinical manifestations of DORV.

steps/14.description: Central cyanosis, typically neonatal or early infantile. It is most severe in the Taussig-Bing (subpulmonary VSD) form, where desaturated systemic venous blood is streamed into the aorta, and in any DORV with significant pulmonary stenosis. Hypercyanotic spells resembling those of tetralogy of Fallot may occur.

evidence.snippet: Consideration should be given to the urgent need for atrial septostomy in a patient who is desaturated and has evidence of a poor cardiac output state.
evidence.explanation: Documents systemic desaturation as a clinical state requiring urgent intervention in DORV; the source describes desaturation rather than using the term hypoxemia, hence PARTIAL.

steps/15.description: Reduced systemic arterial oxygen saturation resulting from obligatory intracardiac mixing, aggravated when pulmonary blood flow is restricted or when streaming directs desaturated blood preferentially to the aorta.

evidence.snippet: Hypoplastic ventricles were present in 39%, pulmonary stenosis was present in 65%, and aortic arch obstruction was present in 24%.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies pulmonary stenosis in 65% of a 393-patient DORV cohort, supporting a FREQUENT frequency band.

steps/16.description: Obstruction of the right ventricular outflow tract, most often from deviation of the muscular outlet septum into the subpulmonary infundibulum, but also valvar or supravalvar. It is the single most common associated lesion and converts an overcirculated DORV into a cyanotic one.

evidence.snippet: leading to subaortic/aortic stenosis, CoA and IAA
evidence.explanation: Names subaortic stenosis as a consequence of the reduced fetal left ventricular outflow that accompanies a subpulmonary VSD; PARTIAL because the source states the association without specifying the obstructing structure.

steps/17.description: Subaortic obstruction produced by posterior deviation of the outlet septum, by a restrictive interventricular communication, or by a long non-contractile intraventricular baffle after repair. It is characteristic of the subpulmonary-VSD (Taussig-Bing) form and is also a recognised late postoperative complication.

evidence.snippet: A wide variety of cardiac malformations of the heart may accompany DORV including coarctation of the aorta (CoA)
evidence.explanation: Directly lists coarctation of the aorta among the malformations accompanying DORV.

evidence.snippet: Hypoplastic ventricles were present in 39%, pulmonary stenosis was present in 65%, and aortic arch obstruction was present in 24%.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies aortic arch obstruction, of which coarctation is the commonest form, in 24% of a large DORV cohort, supporting the OCCASIONAL band.

steps/18.description: Narrowing of the aortic isthmus, part of the spectrum of aortic arch obstruction that accompanies DORV, particularly the Taussig-Bing form in which reduced fetal flow through the systemic outlet limits arch growth.

evidence.snippet: interrupted aortic arch (IAA) and aortic arch obstruction
evidence.explanation: Lists interrupted aortic arch among the cardiac malformations accompanying DORV.

steps/19.description: Complete discontinuity of the aortic arch, the most severe expression of the arch obstruction associated with DORV and particularly with the Taussig-Bing anomaly.

evidence.snippet: the EKG may show right axis deviation with right ventricular hypertrophy
evidence.explanation: Documents right ventricular hypertrophy as an electrocardiographic finding in the commonest DORV subtype.

steps/20.description: Hypertrophy of the morphologic right ventricle, which supports both arterial trunks and is additionally pressure-loaded when outflow obstruction is present. In the Fallot-type subgroup the electrocardiogram shows right axis deviation with right ventricular hypertrophy.

evidence.snippet: patients with subaortic VSD or subpulmonary VSD can have pulmonary over-circulation requiring aggressive diuresis
evidence.explanation: Documents the congestive physiology requiring diuresis; the source describes pulmonary overcirculation and its decongestive treatment rather than naming congestive heart failure, hence PARTIAL.

steps/21.description: Congestive heart failure driven by pulmonary overcirculation and ventricular volume overload when pulmonary outflow is unobstructed; also a late postoperative problem after Rastelli-type repair with conduit obstruction and right ventricular dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: At times, this may lead to the need for respiratory support and intubation.
evidence.explanation: Documents the respiratory decompensation caused by pulmonary overcirculation in DORV, of which tachypnoea is the earliest sign; the source describes escalating respiratory support rather than naming tachypnoea, hence PARTIAL.

steps/22.description: Rapid breathing from pulmonary congestion and increased pulmonary blood flow, typically emerging over the first weeks of life as pulmonary vascular resistance falls.

steps/23.description: Poor and prolonged feeding in infancy, driven by the tachypnoea and increased work of breathing that accompany pulmonary overcirculation. It is the proximate cause of the reduced caloric intake that, with the raised metabolic demand of heart failure, produces failure to thrive in the unrepaired overcirculated forms of DORV.

steps/24.description: Poor weight gain in infancy resulting from the increased metabolic demand of heart failure combined with feeding difficulty, characteristic of the overcirculated forms of DORV before repair.

steps/25.description: Elevated pulmonary arterial pressure from sustained high-flow, high-pressure pulmonary circulation. If repair is delayed, obstructive pulmonary vascular remodelling becomes irreversible and precludes both biventricular repair and Fontan palliation.

evidence.snippet: Hypoplastic ventricles were present in 39%, pulmonary stenosis was present in 65%, and aortic arch obstruction was present in 24%.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies ventricular hypoplasia in 39% of a 393-patient DORV cohort, supporting a FREQUENT frequency band.

evidence.snippet: the LV will show an element of hypoplasia, which can vary from mild to severe
evidence.explanation: Directly documents left ventricular hypoplasia in DORV with a restricted or absent interventricular communication.

steps/26.description: An underdeveloped left ventricle, arising when the interventricular communication is restrictive, remote or absent so that fetal left ventricular filling and ejection are reduced. It is the principal determinant of ineligibility for biventricular repair.

evidence.snippet: Since Van Praagh type III DORV is associated with heterotaxy
evidence.explanation: Directly associates a defined anatomic class of DORV with heterotaxy.

evidence.snippet: laterality defects such as the heterotaxy syndromes of isomerism of the atrial appendages
evidence.explanation: Lists heterotaxy with atrial isomerism among the malformations that accompany DORV.

steps/27.description: Abnormal left-right arrangement of the thoracic and abdominal viscera with atrial isomerism, present in the laterality-associated (Van Praagh type III) form of DORV. Its presence carries additional conduction, splenic and venous anomalies and worsens surgical risk.

evidence.snippet: as well as common AV valves can be found with DORV
evidence.explanation: Documents a common atrioventricular valve, the hallmark of a complete atrioventricular canal defect, as an associated lesion of DORV.

steps/28.description: A common atrioventricular valve with a shared atrioventricular junction, frequently accompanying DORV in the laterality-associated form. Its presence complicates baffle construction and often mandates single-ventricle palliation.

evidence.snippet: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and double-outlet right ventricle (DORV) are conotruncal defects resulting from disturbances of the second heart field and the neural crest, which can occur as isolated malformations or as part of multiorgan syndromes.
evidence.explanation: Places the second-heart-field and neural-crest disturbance causally upstream of the conotruncal alignment defect that produces DORV.

edges/0.description: Deficient or disorganised neural crest and second-heart-field contribution leaves the outflow tract unable to elongate and rotate normally.

edges/1.description: Perturbed conotruncal maturation prevents the normal resorption of the subaortic conal free wall.

evidence.explanation: Shows that randomised looping from a laterality defect yields both DORV and abnormal great-artery position, the alignment failure this edge asserts.

evidence.snippet: In DORV, the subaortic conus frequently persists

edges/9.description: The double-outlet ventriculo-arterial connection is the defining anatomic phenotype.

evidence.snippet: there is almost always an interventricular communication: ventricular septal defect (VSD) or atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD)
evidence.explanation: Documents the near-obligatory interventricular communication that follows from the double-outlet connection.

edges/10.description: Loss of a direct left ventricular arterial outlet makes an interventricular communication obligatory for viable left ventricular egress.
