evidence.snippet: We found that HARP is an ATP-dependent annealing helicase that rewinds single-stranded DNA bubbles that are stably bound by replication protein A.
evidence.explanation: Defines the molecular activity of SMARCAL1/HARP that is lost in SIOD.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of mutant HARP proteins suggests that SIOD is caused by a deficiency in annealing helicase activity.
evidence.explanation: Attributes SIOD to deficient annealing helicase activity of the mutant proteins.

evidence.snippet: The SIOD associated SMARCAL1 mutations affected SMARCAL1 protein expression, stability, subcellular localisation, chromatin binding, and enzymatic activity.
evidence.explanation: Documents the multiple molecular defects produced by SIOD-associated SMARCAL1 mutations.

evidence.snippet: Further, expressing SMARCAL1 missense mutants in Drosophila melanogaster showed that disease severity was inversely proportionate to overall SMARCAL1 activity.
evidence.explanation: In vivo Drosophila assay showing residual SMARCAL1 activity tracks inversely with disease severity.

steps/1.description: Biallelic loss-of-function SMARCAL1 variants abolish or reduce the SMARCAL1 (HARP) protein, an SNF2-family ATP-driven annealing helicase that rewinds RPA-stabilized single-stranded DNA bubbles at replication forks. Disease-associated mutations impair SMARCAL1 expression, stability, chromatin binding, and ATPase/annealing activity, and residual overall SMARCAL1 activity is inversely proportional to disease severity.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, SMARCAL1-deficient cells are hypersensitive to replication stress agents.
evidence.explanation: Documents replication-stress hypersensitivity of SMARCAL1-deficient cells.

evidence.snippet: SMARCAL1-depleted cells display sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents that induce replication fork collapse, and exhibit slower fork recovery and delayed entry into mitosis following S-phase arrest.
evidence.explanation: Documents defective replication fork recovery in SMARCAL1-deficient cells.

evidence.snippet: We did not find evidence of defective NER or NHEJ; however, Smarcal1-deficient mice were hypersensitive to several genotoxic agents.
evidence.explanation: Confirms in vivo hypersensitivity of Smarcal1-deficient mice to genotoxic agents.

evidence.snippet: In renal biopsies from SIOD patients, TUNEL analysis detected marked increases in DNA fragmentation.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates DNA damage accumulation in affected patient tissue.

steps/2.description: SMARCAL1-deficient cells activate the DNA damage response during S phase without exogenous genotoxins, show slower replication fork recovery and delayed mitotic entry after S-phase arrest, and are hypersensitive to replication stress and DNA-damaging agents in vitro and in vivo. This replication stress preferentially compromises highly proliferative compartments (growth plate, glomerulus, thymus/lymphocytes, marrow) and underlies the hypersensitivity to genotoxic therapies observed clinically.

evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that the T cells of SIOD patients have undetectable levels of protein and mRNA for the IL-7 receptor alpha chain (IL7Rα) and are unresponsive to stimulation with IL-7, indicating a loss of functional receptor.
evidence.explanation: Documents the loss of functional IL-7 receptor on SIOD T cells.

evidence.snippet: We propose therefore that the lack of IL7Rα expression, associated with hypermethylation of the IL7R promoter, in T cells and possibly their earlier progenitors, restricts T-cell development in SIOD patients.
evidence.explanation: Proposes epigenetic IL7R silencing as the mechanism restricting T-cell development.

evidence.snippet: Its hallmarks are severe hypogammaglobulinemia requiring immunoglobulin substitution, as well as impaired function of the thymus resulting in overall T cell lymphopenia
evidence.explanation: Attributes the T-cell lymphopenia to impaired thymic function and notes the accompanying humoral deficiency.

steps/3.description: T-cell production fails at the level of the thymus. SIOD patient T cells have undetectable IL-7 receptor alpha chain (IL7Rα) protein and mRNA with hypermethylation of the IL7R promoter and are unresponsive to IL-7, restricting T-cell development; residual peripheral T cells are skewed to mature/memory phenotypes with exhaustion features. B-cell numbers and immunoglobulins are comparatively preserved early, though hypogammaglobulinemia — aggravated by nephrotic protein loss — is a hallmark of the combined immunodeficiency.

evidence.snippet: As predicted by the clinical course, T cell deficiency in peripheral lymphoid organs, defective chondrogenesis, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, cerebral ischaemic lesions and premature atherosclerosis were identified.
evidence.explanation: Autopsy confirmation of defective chondrogenesis in SIOD.

evidence.snippet: A regulatory role for the SMARCAL1 protein in the proliferation of chondrocytes, lymphocytes and spermatozoa, as well as in the development or maintenance of cardiomyocytes and in vascular homoeostasis, is suggested.
evidence.explanation: Implicates SMARCAL1 in chondrocyte proliferation, the cellular basis of the impaired chondrogenesis.

steps/4.description: Defective chondrogenesis with loss of proliferating growth-plate chondrocytes underlies the spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia. Autopsy studies identify defective chondrogenesis and suggest a regulatory role for SMARCAL1 in chondrocyte proliferation; the resulting dysplasia predominantly involves the vertebrae, pelvis, and capital femoral epiphyses, producing short-trunk disproportionate growth failure.

evidence.snippet: Our analysis of SIOD patient renal biopsies demonstrates the tip and collapsing variants of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS).
evidence.explanation: Histological characterization of the SIOD renal lesion.

evidence.snippet: Additionally, electron microscopy revealed numerous glomerular abnormalities most notably in the podocyte and Bowman's capsule.
evidence.explanation: Ultrastructural localization of the injury to the podocyte.

evidence.snippet: The nephrotic syndrome in SIOD is a podocytopathy that usually progresses to focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and end-stage kidney disease.
evidence.explanation: Frames the SIOD nephropathy as a podocytopathy progressing through FSGS to end-stage kidney disease.

steps/5.description: The nephropathy of SIOD is a podocytopathy. SMARCAL1 is expressed in podocytes and glomerular endothelial cells; patient biopsies show the tip and collapsing variants of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis with ultrastructural podocyte and Bowman's-capsule abnormalities, and the podocytopathy usually progresses through FSGS to end-stage kidney disease.

evidence.snippet: The arteriosclerosis was characterized by intimal and medial hyperplasia, smooth muscle cell hyperplasia and fragmented and disorganized elastin fibers, and the pulmonary disease was characterized by panlobular enlargement of air spaces.
evidence.explanation: Histopathological definition of the vascular and pulmonary lesions.

evidence.snippet: Consistent with a cell autonomous disorder, SMARCAL1 was expressed in arterial and lung tissue, and both the aorta and lung of SIOD patients had reduced expression of elastin and alterations in the expression of regulators of elastin gene expression.
evidence.explanation: Attributes the lesions to reduced elastogenesis in SMARCAL1-deficient tissue.

steps/6.description: Reduced elastin expression in aorta and lung, with altered expression of regulators of elastin gene expression, produces an arteriosclerosis characterized by intimal and medial hyperplasia, smooth muscle cell hyperplasia and fragmented, disorganized elastin fibers, and an emphysema-like panlobular enlargement of air spaces. Vascular disease — including premature atherosclerosis and cerebral vaso-occlusion — is a major cause of morbidity and mortality.

evidence.snippet: Schimke immunoosseous dysplasia (SIOD) is characterized by spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia (SED) resulting in short stature, nephropathy, and T cell deficiency.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews names SED-related short stature as a defining (characterizing) feature, supporting the very-frequent band.

evidence.snippet: The main clinical findings are spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia with disproportionate growth restriction, defective cellular immunity, and steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome secondary to biopsy proven FSGS leading to ESRF.
evidence.explanation: Documents the disproportionate growth restriction.

steps/7.description: Growth failure with short-trunk disproportionate short stature is the presenting feature in most patients, produced by the spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia; intrauterine growth retardation frequently precedes it.

evidence.snippet: Radiographic manifestations of SED include ovoid and mildly flattened vertebral bodies, small ilia with shallow dysplastic acetabular fossae, and small deformed capital femoral epiphyses.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews radiographic definition of the SED.

evidence.snippet: Schimke immunoosseous dysplasia (SIOD) is characterized by spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia (SED) resulting in short stature, nephropathy, and T cell deficiency.
evidence.explanation: SED is a defining feature of the disease, supporting the very-frequent band.

evidence.snippet: We found that patients with SMARCAL1 mutations have a spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia (SED) essentially limited to the spine, pelvis, capital femoral epiphyses, and possibly the sella turcica, whereas the hands and other long bones are basically normal.
evidence.explanation: Defines the anatomical distribution of the SED.

steps/8.description: The skeletal dysplasia is essentially limited to the spine, pelvis, and capital femoral epiphyses: ovoid and mildly flattened vertebral bodies, small ilia with shallow dysplastic acetabular fossae, and small deformed capital femoral epiphyses; hands and other long bones are largely normal. Osteopenia/osteoporosis and degenerative hip disease develop in older patients.

evidence.snippet: Nearly all affected individuals have progressive steroid-resistant nephropathy, usually developing within five years of the diagnosis of growth failure and terminating with end-stage renal disease.
evidence.explanation: "Nearly all" supports the very-frequent band for steroid-resistant nephropathy.

evidence.snippet: The main clinical findings are spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia with disproportionate growth restriction, defective cellular immunity, and steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome secondary to biopsy proven FSGS leading to ESRF.
evidence.explanation: Names steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome as a main finding.

steps/9.description: Nearly all patients develop progressive steroid-resistant nephropathy — clinically a nephrotic syndrome unresponsive to corticosteroids — usually within five years of the diagnosis of growth failure.

evidence.snippet: Our analysis of SIOD patient renal biopsies demonstrates the tip and collapsing variants of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS).
evidence.explanation: Biopsy demonstration of FSGS variants in SIOD.

evidence.snippet: As predicted by the clinical course, T cell deficiency in peripheral lymphoid organs, defective chondrogenesis, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, cerebral ischaemic lesions and premature atherosclerosis were identified.
evidence.explanation: Autopsy confirmation of FSGS.

steps/10.description: Renal biopsy shows FSGS — characteristically the tip and collapsing variants — as the histological substrate of the nephrotic syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Nearly all affected individuals have progressive steroid-resistant nephropathy, usually developing within five years of the diagnosis of growth failure and terminating with end-stage renal disease.
evidence.explanation: "Nearly all" individuals progress to end-stage renal disease, supporting the very-frequent band.

steps/11.description: The nephropathy terminates in end-stage renal disease in nearly all affected individuals, necessitating renal replacement therapy or transplantation.

evidence.snippet: The majority of tested individuals have T cell deficiency and an associated risk for opportunistic infection, a common cause of death.
evidence.explanation: "The majority of tested individuals" supports the frequent band for T-cell deficiency.

evidence.snippet: Its hallmarks are severe hypogammaglobulinemia requiring immunoglobulin substitution, as well as impaired function of the thymus resulting in overall T cell lymphopenia
evidence.explanation: Documents the overall T-cell lymphopenia.

steps/12.description: Progressive T-cell lymphopenia from impaired thymic output is the core immunological defect; residual T cells lack IL7Rα, are skewed toward memory phenotypes, and show features of exhaustion.

evidence.snippet: The characteristic features of SIOD include 1) short stature with hyperpigmented macules and an unusual facies, 2) proteinuria with progressive renal failure, 3) lymphopenia with recurrent infections, and 4) cerebral ischaemia.
evidence.explanation: Recurrent infections are one of the characteristic features.

evidence.snippet: The majority of tested individuals have T cell deficiency and an associated risk for opportunistic infection, a common cause of death.
evidence.explanation: Documents the associated opportunistic-infection risk and its contribution to mortality.

steps/13.description: Recurrent bacterial, viral, and fungal infections — including opportunistic infections — result from the combined T-cell and humoral deficiency and are a leading cause of death.

evidence.snippet: We emphasize the high incidence of cerebral ischaemia and ocular abnormalities, define the high incidence of thyroid dysfunction and blood cytopenia, and confirm the absence of effective and durable medical therapies.
evidence.explanation: Reports a high incidence of cerebral ischemia, supporting the frequent band.

evidence.snippet: Individuals affected with SIOD usually die within the first two decades of life from infections (23%), stroke (17%), renal failure (15%), pulmonary hypertension and congestive heart failure (15%), complications of organ transplantation (9%), complications of lymphoproliferative disease (9%), gastrointestinal bleeding (6%), bone marrow failure (3%), and unspecified acute restrictive lung disease (3%)
evidence.explanation: Stroke accounts for 17% of deaths in SIOD.

steps/14.description: Transient ischemic attacks and strokes on the background of the cerebral arteriopathy occur at high incidence; stroke accounts for about 17% of deaths.

evidence.snippet: Thirty-two of 63 patients had signs of arteriosclerosis and 3 of 51 had signs of emphysema.
evidence.explanation: 32 of 63 patients (51%) had arteriosclerosis, supporting the frequent band.

evidence.snippet: As predicted by the clinical course, T cell deficiency in peripheral lymphoid organs, defective chondrogenesis, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, cerebral ischaemic lesions and premature atherosclerosis were identified.
evidence.explanation: Autopsy confirmation of premature atherosclerosis.

steps/15.description: Premature, elastin-deficient arteriosclerosis/atherosclerosis was present in about half of evaluable patients in the largest vascular series and is confirmed at autopsy.

evidence.snippet: Among 71 SIOD patients, three had non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) and one had osteosarcoma.
evidence.explanation: 3 of 71 patients (4%) had NHL, supporting the very-rare (1-4%) band while documenting the predisposition.

steps/16.description: SIOD carries an increased prevalence of malignancy, most commonly non-Hodgkin lymphoma (3 of 71 patients, with one osteosarcoma), consistent with the underlying genome instability.

evidence.snippet: Thus, SMARCAL1 is a replication stress response protein, and the pleiotropic phenotypes of SIOD are at least partly due to defects in genome maintenance during DNA replication.
evidence.explanation: Directly links SMARCAL1 loss to defective genome maintenance during replication as the proximate disease mechanism.

edges/1.description: Loss of the annealing helicase removes a replication stress response protein that maintains genome integrity at stalled replication forks, producing replication-associated DNA damage.

evidence.snippet: Consistent with a cell autonomous disorder, SMARCAL1 was expressed in arterial and lung tissue, and both the aorta and lung of SIOD patients had reduced expression of elastin and alterations in the expression of regulators of elastin gene expression.
evidence.explanation: Connects SMARCAL1 deficiency in vascular tissue to reduced elastin expression.

edges/2.description: SMARCAL1 is expressed in arterial and lung tissue, and SMARCAL1-deficient aorta and lung show reduced elastin expression with altered expression of elastin-gene regulators; the intermediate steps from SMARCAL1 loss to the transcriptional deficit are not established.

evidence.snippet: Also, CPT-11, etoposide, and HU caused decreased growth and loss of growth plate chondrocytes.
evidence.explanation: Genotoxic stress in Smarcal1-deficient mice produces growth-plate chondrocyte loss and decreased growth, linking replication stress to the skeletal arm.

edges/3.description: Replication stress compromises proliferating growth-plate chondrocytes; genotoxic agents reproduce growth-plate chondrocyte loss in Smarcal1-deficient mice.

evidence.snippet: Further, we suggest that disruptions in genomic integrity during fetal kidney development contribute to the pathogenesis of FSGS in SIOD patients.
evidence.explanation: Proposes genomic-integrity disruption as the driver of FSGS in SIOD kidneys.

edges/4.description: Genomic instability in the developing and mature kidney, evidenced by markedly increased DNA fragmentation in patient renal biopsies, is proposed to drive the podocytopathy.

evidence.snippet: UV light irradiation caused a severe increase in the apoptosis of T cells
evidence.explanation: Patient T cells are hypersensitive to DNA damage, linking the genome-maintenance defect to the T-cell compartment.

edges/5.description: Replication and DNA-damage stress in thymocytes and T cells, together with epigenetic silencing of IL7R, restricts T-cell production; patient T cells show markedly increased apoptosis after DNA damage.

evidence.snippet: Among 71 SIOD patients, three had non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) and one had osteosarcoma.
evidence.explanation: Documents the increased prevalence of NHL in a large SIOD cohort, interpreted by the authors as a consequence of the DNA stress response defect.

edges/6.description: Genome instability predisposes to malignancy; NHL is the most commonly reported cancer in SIOD cohorts.

evidence.snippet: We found that patients with SMARCAL1 mutations have a spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia (SED) essentially limited to the spine, pelvis, capital femoral epiphyses, and possibly the sella turcica, whereas the hands and other long bones are basically normal.
evidence.explanation: Radiographic definition of the SED produced by the skeletal arm of the disease.

edges/7.description: Defective chondrogenesis of vertebral and proximal epiphyseal growth centers produces the characteristic spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia.

evidence.snippet: the spondyloepiphyseal dysplasias (SEDs) are characterized by primary involvement of the vertebrae and proximal epiphyseal centers resulting in a short-trunk disproportionate dwarfism
evidence.explanation: Explains how the SED yields disproportionate short-trunk short stature.

edges/8.description: The spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, with primary involvement of vertebrae and proximal epiphyses, results in short-trunk disproportionate growth failure.

evidence.snippet: Our analysis of SIOD patient renal biopsies demonstrates the tip and collapsing variants of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS).
evidence.explanation: Biopsy demonstration of FSGS as the renal lesion of SIOD.

edges/9.description: Podocyte injury and loss produce segmental scarring of glomeruli — the tip and collapsing FSGS variants seen on biopsy.

evidence.snippet: The main clinical findings are spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia with disproportionate growth restriction, defective cellular immunity, and steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome secondary to biopsy proven FSGS leading to ESRF.
evidence.explanation: Attributes the steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome to biopsy-proven FSGS.

edges/10.description: The podocytopathy manifests clinically as proteinuria and nephrotic syndrome that does not respond to corticosteroids.

evidence.snippet: Nearly all affected individuals have progressive steroid-resistant nephropathy, usually developing within five years of the diagnosis of growth failure and terminating with end-stage renal disease.
evidence.explanation: Documents the near-universal progression to end-stage renal disease.

edges/11.description: The steroid-resistant nephropathy progresses through FSGS to end-stage renal disease, usually within five years of the diagnosis of growth failure.

evidence.snippet: Its hallmarks are severe hypogammaglobulinemia requiring immunoglobulin substitution, as well as impaired function of the thymus resulting in overall T cell lymphopenia
evidence.explanation: Links impaired thymic function to the overall T-cell lymphopenia.

edges/12.description: Restricted thymic T-cell development produces the characteristic progressive T-cell lymphopenia.

evidence.snippet: Although recurrent infection, due to T-cell deficiency, is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, the etiology of the T-cell immunodeficiency is unclear.
evidence.explanation: States that recurrent infection results from the T-cell deficiency and drives morbidity and mortality.

edges/13.description: T-cell deficiency, aggravated by antibody loss from nephrotic syndrome and immunosuppressive treatment, causes recurrent and opportunistic infections — the leading cause of death.

evidence.snippet: Thirty-two of 63 patients had signs of arteriosclerosis and 3 of 51 had signs of emphysema.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies arteriosclerosis prevalence in the SIOD cohort.

edges/14.description: The elastin-deficient arteriopathy manifests as premature atherosclerosis/arteriosclerosis, present in about half of evaluable patients.

evidence.snippet: As predicted by the clinical course, T cell deficiency in peripheral lymphoid organs, defective chondrogenesis, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, cerebral ischaemic lesions and premature atherosclerosis were identified.
evidence.explanation: Autopsy demonstration of cerebral ischemic lesions together with premature atherosclerosis.

edges/15.description: Cerebral vaso-occlusive disease on the background of the arteriopathy produces transient ischemic attacks and strokes.

evidence.snippet: Using genome-wide linkage mapping and a positional candidate approach, we determined that mutations in SMARCAL1 (SWI/SNF2-related, matrix-associated, actin-dependent regulator of chromatin, subfamily a-like 1), are responsible for SIOD.
evidence.explanation: Establishes SMARCAL1 as the causative gene.

evidence.snippet: affected individuals from 13 of 23 families with severe disease had two alleles with nonsense, frameshift or splicing mutations, whereas affected individuals from 3 of 3 families with milder disease had a missense mutation on each allele
evidence.explanation: Documents the genotype-severity correlation.

evidence.snippet: the most common was c.2542G>T, resulting in premature translation termination (p.E848*), and it was found in 14 patients either in a homozygous (four patients) or compound-heterozygous (10 patients) state
evidence.explanation: Documents the recurrent founder truncating variant.

evidence.snippet: Biallelic mutations in swi/snf-related, matrix-associated, actin-dependent regulator of chromatin, subfamily a-like 1 (SMARCAL1) are the only identified cause of SIOD, but approximately half of patients referred for molecular studies do not have detectable mutations in SMARCAL1.
evidence.explanation: SMARCAL1 is the only identified cause; a fraction of clinically similar patients remain unexplained.

genes/0.notes: SMARCAL1 (HARP) encodes an SNF2-family ATP-driven annealing helicase. A Russian founder variant, c.2542G>T (p.E848*), accounted for 14 of 19 genotyped patients in the largest single-centre series. Approximately half of patients referred with an SIOD-like phenotype have no detectable SMARCAL1 mutation, suggesting genetic heterogeneity of the broader phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Concerning ESRF, kidney transplantation is the therapy of choice since FSGS does not recur in the graft.
evidence.explanation: Establishes kidney transplantation as the therapy of choice.

evidence.snippet: renal transplantation as indicated using mild immunosuppressive therapy
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews management recommendation for renal transplantation.

treatments/0.description: Kidney transplantation is the therapy of choice for the end-stage renal failure of SIOD because FSGS does not recur in the graft; GeneReviews recommends transplantation with mild immunosuppressive therapy given the underlying immunodeficiency.

evidence.snippet: Concerning ESRF, kidney transplantation is the therapy of choice since FSGS does not recur in the graft.
evidence.explanation: Transplantation bypasses the intrinsic podocytopathy, and the disease does not recur in donor tissue.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Transplantation replaces the sclerosed kidney rather than correcting the SMARCAL1 defect; because the podocytopathy is cell-autonomous, FSGS does not recur in the donor graft.

evidence.snippet: We have found that post-renal transplantation immunosuppressive monotherapy results in a good outcome with a reduced number of severe infections.
evidence.explanation: Supports monotherapy maintenance immunosuppression in SIOD.

evidence.snippet: Under conventional immunosuppressive regimens some SIOD patients have developed severe disseminated cutaneous papilloma virus infections or EBV associated lymphoproliferative disease.
evidence.explanation: Documents the infectious complications of conventional-intensity immunosuppression that motivate minimization.

treatments/1.description: Because of the underlying T-cell immunodeficiency, conventional combination immunosuppression after renal transplantation has led to severe disseminated cutaneous papillomavirus infections and EBV-associated lymphoproliferative disease; immunosuppressive monotherapy maintenance gives good graft outcomes with fewer severe infections, and limited immunosuppression appears possible without increased rejection risk.

evidence.snippet: We find that only one patient survived the transplantation procedure and that the existing indicators of a good prognosis for bone marrow transplantation were not predictive in this small cohort.
evidence.explanation: Documents the very high procedure-related mortality of early BMT in SIOD, the stated caveat for this treatment.

evidence.snippet: Previously, four of five patients with SIOD who underwent HSCT after myeloablative conditioning died from HSCT-related causes, including infections and GVHD
evidence.explanation: Attributes the historical HSCT deaths to myeloablative-conditioning-era protocols.

evidence.snippet: hematopoietic stem cell transplantation as indicated
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews lists HSCT among management options as indicated.

treatments/2.description: HSCT is a potential definitive therapy for the T-cell immunodeficiency and bone marrow failure, but the historical experience is poor: only one of the first five transplanted patients survived, with the four deaths following myeloablative conditioning — a toxicity plausibly linked to the hypersensitivity of SMARCAL1-deficient cells to DNA-damaging agents. Reduced-intensity conditioning with alpha-beta T-cell-depleted haploidentical grafts underlies the more recent successes.

evidence.snippet: Full donor hematopoietic chimerism and functional ex vivo T-cell tolerance was achieved, and the patients continued to have normal renal function without immunosuppression at 22 to 34 months after kidney transplantation.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates full donor hematopoietic reconstitution in SIOD patients after reduced-intensity haploidentical HSCT.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Successful engraftment replaces the SMARCAL1-deficient hematopoietic compartment, restoring T-cell immunity; full donor chimerism has been achieved with reduced-intensity haploidentical protocols.

evidence.snippet: Full donor hematopoietic chimerism and functional ex vivo T-cell tolerance was achieved, and the patients continued to have normal renal function without immunosuppression at 22 to 34 months after kidney transplantation.
evidence.explanation: Reports the immunosuppression-free outcome of sequential stem cell-kidney transplantation in three SIOD patients.

treatments/3.description: Sequential transplantation of alpha-beta T-cell-depleted, CD19 B-cell-depleted haploidentical hematopoietic stem cells followed by a kidney from the same donor established full donor chimerism and immune tolerance in three children with SIOD, who maintained normal renal function without any immunosuppression at 22 to 34 months — addressing the immunodeficiency and the renal failure with a single donor while eliminating post-transplant immunosuppression.

evidence.snippet: Full donor hematopoietic chimerism and functional ex vivo T-cell tolerance was achieved, and the patients continued to have normal renal function without immunosuppression at 22 to 34 months after kidney transplantation.
evidence.explanation: Documents immune reconstitution with donor chimerism and tolerance.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: The haploidentical HSCT arm replaces the defective hematopoietic and immune compartment.

evidence.snippet: Each patient received sequential transplants of αβ T-cell-depleted and CD19 B-cell-depleted haploidentical hematopoietic stem cells and a kidney from the same donor.
evidence.explanation: Describes the sequential same-donor stem cell and kidney transplantation strategy.

treatments/3/targets/1.description: The same-donor kidney replaces the failed organ, and the induced tolerance removes the need for maintenance immunosuppression.

evidence.snippet: acyclovir for recurrent herpetic infections and/or shingles; imiquimod and cidofovir for severe disseminated cutaneous papilloma virus infections
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews anti-infective supportive measures.

evidence.snippet: Avoid hypertension; heat, stress, and lack of sleep; and live attenuated immunizations in those who are T cell deficient. Use DNA-damaging anti-cancer therapies with caution due to evidence of susceptibility to genotoxic agents.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews agents/circumstances to avoid, including the genotoxic caution that follows from the replication-stress mechanism.

treatments/4.description: Multidisciplinary supportive care includes acyclovir for recurrent herpetic infections, imiquimod and cidofovir for severe disseminated cutaneous papillomavirus infections, G-CSF or GM-CSF for neutropenia, levothyroxine for hypothyroidism, agents that improve blood flow or reduce coagulability for ischemic events, and blood-pressure control. Live-attenuated vaccines should be avoided in T-cell-deficient patients; hypertension, heat, stress, and sleep deprivation can precipitate neurovascular events; and DNA-damaging anti-cancer therapies must be used with caution given the genotoxic hypersensitivity.

evidence.snippet: RAG1 and RAG2, are DNA recombinases that mediate DNA recombination process and ensure the somatic diversification of immunoglobulin and TCR genes during B-cell and T-cell development, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Supports the initiating step of this node — RAG-mediated recombination of antigen-receptor genes in developing B and T cells.

evidence.snippet: In the absence of VDJ recombination, T cell undergoes apoptosis.
evidence.explanation: Supports the causal step from failed V(D)J recombination to loss of developing T cells.

evidence.snippet: DCLRE1C encodes ARTEMIS, a nuclease which is single-stranded with- 5′-3′ exonuclease potential and endonuclease activity over 5′ and 3′ ends. It is essential for V(D)J rearrangement and for DNA repair.
evidence.explanation: Supports the Artemis arm of this node, covering both hairpin processing during recombination and general DNA repair.

evidence.snippet: Patients with this form of SCID are sensitive to ionizing radiation and chemotherapeutic agents.
evidence.explanation: Supports the cellular radiosensitivity this node attributes specifically to Artemis loss.

evidence.snippet: Radiosensitive T-B- severe combined immunodeficiency (RS-SCID) is caused by defects in the nonhomologous end-joining (NHEJ) DNA repair pathway, which results in failure of functional V(D)J recombination.
evidence.explanation: Supports extending this node to the end-joining components, and the T-B-NK+ immunophenotype they share with Artemis deficiency.

evidence.snippet: DNA ligase IV functions in DNA nonhomologous end-joining and V(D)J recombination.
evidence.explanation: Supports placing LIG4 at the ligation step of the same end-joining pathway this node models.

steps/13.description: In RAG1, RAG2, DCLRE1C (Artemis), PRKDC (DNA-PKcs), and LIG4 (DNA ligase IV) deficiency, the machinery that assembles antigen-receptor genes is impaired. RAG1/RAG2 initiate site-specific DNA cleavage during V(D)J recombination; Artemis opens the resulting DNA hairpins as part of non-homologous end-joining; DNA-PKcs activates Artemis for that step; and DNA ligase IV seals the repaired ends. Failure to recombine T-cell (and B-cell) receptor genes arrests lymphocyte development (T-B-NK+). Loss of any of the three end-joining components additionally confers cellular radiosensitivity, which is what makes the molecular diagnosis matter before transplant conditioning.

evidence.snippet: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency is a systemic purine metabolic disorder that primarily affects lymphocyte development, viability, and function.
evidence.explanation: ADA deficiency causes toxic purine-metabolite accumulation that impairs lymphocyte development, viability, and function.

evidence.snippet: Deficiency of ADA causes accumulation of adenosine, deoxyadenosine, and 2′-O-methyladenosine resulting in lymphocyte apoptosis, causing the absence of T cell function.
evidence.explanation: Names the accumulating metabolites bound as chemical entities on this node and supplies the intermediate step this node asserts — lymphocyte apoptosis leading to loss of T-cell function.

evidence.snippet: total red blood cell deoxyadenosine nucleotides (dAXP) and, if on ERT, plasma ADA activity
evidence.explanation: Deoxyadenosine nucleotides (dAXP) are the accumulating phosphorylated species this node refers to, and are the monitored disease marker.

steps/14.description: In ADA deficiency, loss of adenosine deaminase activity causes accumulation of adenosine and especially deoxyadenosine (and intracellular dATP), which are lymphotoxic and impair lymphocyte development, viability, and function. The metabolic toxicity affects all lymphoid lineages, producing a T-B-NK- immunophenotype.

evidence.snippet: Adenylate kinases are involved in cellular and mitochondrial energy homeostasis.
evidence.explanation: Supports the bioenergetic function whose loss initiates this node.

evidence.snippet: Deficiency of AK2 is associated with lack of innate and adaptive immunity.
evidence.explanation: Supports the claim that this mechanism removes innate immunity as well as adaptive immunity.

evidence.snippet: Reticular dysgenesis is the most serious type of SCID that is associated with absent granulocytes, lymphocytes, hypoplasia of the primary and secondary lymphoid organs and fatal septicemia within days after birth.
evidence.explanation: Supports the simultaneous granulocyte and lymphocyte failure and the lymphoid-organ hypoplasia this node produces.

steps/15.description: In reticular dysgenesis, loss of adenylate kinase 2 disrupts cellular and mitochondrial energy homeostasis in haematopoietic precursors themselves. Because the lesion is bioenergetic rather than lymphoid-specific, both myeloid and lymphoid output fail: granulocytes are absent alongside lymphocytes, and innate as well as adaptive immunity is lost. This is the one SCID mechanism class in this entry whose consequences extend outside the lymphoid lineage.

evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of typical and atypical X-SCID is established in a male proband with suggestive findings and a hemizygous pathogenic variant in IL2RG identified by molecular genetic testing.
evidence.explanation: IL2RG common gamma-chain loss underlies X-linked SCID, the cytokine-signaling form of disrupted T-cell development.

evidence.snippet: The gamma portion of IL2R is important for the development of T and NK cells through cytokines IL2 and IL15, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Supports the mechanism claimed by this node — that common gamma-chain cytokine signalling drives both T- and NK-cell development, so its loss gives the T-B+NK- phenotype.

evidence.snippet: JAK3 plays a pivotal role in cytokine receptor cell signalling.
evidence.explanation: Supports placing JAK3 in the same cytokine-receptor signalling node as IL2RG.

evidence.snippet: The encoded protein is expressed on the lymphoid lineage and is required during T cell development during early stage and for proliferation and survival of T cells in the periphery.
evidence.explanation: Supports the IL-7 receptor arm of this node, and specifically the claim that the signal drives early thymocyte survival and proliferation.

steps/16.description: In X-linked SCID, JAK3 deficiency, and IL7R deficiency, loss-of-function in the common gamma chain (IL2RG), its associated kinase JAK3, or the IL-7 receptor alpha chain abolishes IL-7-dependent JAK-STAT signaling that drives early thymocyte survival and proliferation, blocking T-cell development. IL2RG and JAK3 defects additionally abrogate NK-cell development (T-B+NK-), whereas IL7R defects spare B and NK cells (T-B+NK+).

evidence.snippet: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) is a ubiquitously expressed metabolic enzyme that plays an integral role in numerous cellular processes
evidence.explanation: Establishes the premise this node rests on — that the enzyme is not lymphoid-restricted, so its loss is not either.

evidence.snippet: 2′deoxyadenosine irreversibly inactivates S-adenosyl-l-homocysteine (SAH) hydrolase
evidence.explanation: Supports the decreased adenosylhomocysteinase activity bound on this node.

evidence.snippet: Inhibition of SAH hydrolase prevents hydrolysis of SAH, and the accumulated SAH inhibits transmethylation reactions
evidence.explanation: Supports the increased S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine and the decreased methylation bound on this node.

evidence.snippet: dATP is an inhibitor of ribonucleotide reductase that is necessary for deoxynucleotide synthesis, and its inhibition depletes the intracellular deoxynucleotide pool
evidence.explanation: Supports the decreased ribonucleotide reductase activity and the impaired DNA replication bound on this node.

steps/17.description: Because adenosine deaminase is ubiquitously expressed, the deoxyadenosine and dATP that accumulate in its absence are not confined to thymocytes. Two of the same molecular routes that damage developing lymphocytes operate in non-lymphoid cells: 2'-deoxyadenosine irreversibly inactivates S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase, so S-adenosylhomocysteine accumulates and inhibits transmethylation; and dATP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, depleting the deoxynucleotide pool and impairing DNA synthesis in any proliferating cell. This node is the entry point for the extra-immune features of ADA deficiency — neurocognitive, auditory, skeletal, pulmonary and hepatic — which none of the other five SCID subtypes in this entry share.

evidence.snippet: Homozygous mutations in CD3D and CD3E genes lead to a complete block in T-cell development and thus to an early-onset severe combined immunodeficiency phenotype.
evidence.explanation: Supports this node's claim that loss of a CD3 invariant chain blocks T-cell development and produces SCID.

evidence.snippet: Thymic studies have shown that the defect in T-cell development occurs at the transition between 'double-negative' and 'double-positive' thymocytes.
evidence.explanation: Sources the thymocyte stage at which this node places the arrest, and the thymocyte cell type bound here.

evidence.snippet: Linker for activation of T cells (LAT) is a transmembrane adaptor signaling molecule that is part of the TCR complex and essential for T-cell development, as demonstrated by LAT-deficient mice, which show a complete lack of peripheral T cells.
evidence.explanation: Sources the T-cell receptor signaling pathway bound to this node, and LAT's position within the receptor complex.

steps/18.description: In CD3D and LAT deficiency signalling through the pre-T-cell receptor and T-cell receptor fails at or immediately below the receptor, by two different routes. CD3delta is an invariant chain of the complex itself, so its loss leaves no signalling-competent receptor to assemble; LAT is the transmembrane adaptor that propagates the signal from a receptor that is intact, so its loss leaves the receptor silent. Thymocyte development arrests at the double-negative to double-positive transition, giving a T-B+NK+ immunophenotype. This is a fifth mechanism class alongside cytokine receptor signaling, V(D)J recombination and DNA repair, purine metabolism, and haematopoietic precursor survival, and it is the class the CD45/PTPRC and other CD3-chain deficiencies also belong to.

evidence.snippet: Our findings establish a function for coronin 1A in T cell egress, identify a surface of coronin involved in Arp2/3 regulation and demonstrate that actin regulation is a biological process defective in human and mouse severe combined immunodeficiency.
evidence.explanation: Sources both processes bound to this node - thymocyte egress and actin regulation - and their status as a human SCID mechanism.

evidence.snippet: The discovery of another coronin 1A mutant during an N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea-mutagenesis screen for T cell-lymphopenic mice prompted us to evaluate a T cell-deficient, B cell-sufficient and natural killer cell-sufficient patient with severe combined immunodeficiency, whom we found had mutations in both CORO1A alleles.
evidence.explanation: Sources the T-B+NK+ immunophenotype this node asserts, in the index human patient.

evidence.snippet: Mice carrying the recessive locus for peripheral T cell deficiency (Ptcd) have a block in thymic egress, but the mechanism responsible is undefined.
evidence.explanation: The mouse result this node's egress-rather-than-development placement rests on; recorded as model-organism evidence because the human report does not state where the block sits.

evidence.snippet: the E26K mutation does not phenocopy the Coro1A deficient state
evidence.explanation: Distinguishes the gain-of-function Ptcd allele from the null state, which in mice reduces mature thymocyte survival; the node's description and its ABNORMAL Arp2/3 binding modifier cover both alleles for this reason.

evidence.snippet: The identification of a patient with a peripheral T cell deficiency who lacks expression of Coro1A strongly suggests that Coro1A has similar functions in humans as in mice.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the human disease is the null state, not the Ptcd gain-of-function allele.

steps/19.description: In coronin-1A deficiency the actin regulation required for thymocytes to leave the thymus and for peripheral T cells to survive is lost, so T cells do not populate the periphery. The two mouse alleles show the two halves of this separately. The Ptcd strain carries an E26K gain-of-function substitution that increases coronin-1A inhibition of Arp2/3 and blocks thymic egress; Coro1a-null mice, which match the patient's absent protein, instead lose mature thymocytes through reduced survival. Neither is a block in thymocyte development, which is the basis for placing this node beside the developmental block rather than within it.

evidence.snippet: Severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) results from defects in the differentiation of hematopoietic stem cells into mature T lymphocytes, with additional lymphoid lineages affected in particular genotypes.
evidence.explanation: SCID converges on failed differentiation of hematopoietic stem cells into mature T lymphocytes, with additional lineages affected by genotype.

steps/20.description: The convergent consequence of all SCID subtypes is failure of hematopoietic stem cells to differentiate into mature, functional T lymphocytes in the thymus, yielding absent or severely reduced autologous T cells. Depending on the genetic lesion, B and/or NK lineages are also affected.

evidence.snippet: Characteristic immune abnormalities are lymphocytopenia (low numbers of T, B, and NK cells) combined with the absence of both humoral and cellular immune function.
evidence.explanation: SCID produces absence of both humoral and cellular immune function, the loss of adaptive immunity.

steps/21.description: Without functional T cells (and often B cells), the patient cannot mount protective cellular or humoral adaptive immune responses, leaving the infant susceptible to overwhelming bacterial, viral, fungal, and protozoal infection.

evidence.snippet: Severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) results from defects in the differentiation of hematopoietic stem cells into mature T lymphocytes, with additional lymphoid lineages affected in particular genotypes.
evidence.explanation: SCID is defined by combined defects of adaptive immunity arising from failed T-lymphocyte differentiation.

steps/22.description: Profound combined defect of cellular and humoral adaptive immunity is the defining feature.

evidence.snippet: Characteristic immune abnormalities are lymphocytopenia (low numbers of T, B, and NK cells) combined with the absence of both humoral and cellular immune function.
evidence.explanation: SCID features absence of cellular immune function.

steps/23.description: Cell-mediated immune responses are absent owing to loss of functional T lymphocytes.

evidence.snippet: Clinical manifestations are characterised by recurrent and severe bacterial, viral, and fungal opportunistic infections that start from early infancy period.
evidence.explanation: Recurrent severe opportunistic infections from early infancy are the cardinal clinical feature of SCID.

steps/24.description: Recurrent, severe, and opportunistic bacterial, viral, fungal, and protozoal infections beginning in early infancy.

evidence.snippet: Untreated ADA-SCID presents as life-threatening opportunistic illnesses in the first weeks to months of life with poor linear growth and weight gain secondary to persistent diarrhea, extensive dermatitis, and recurrent pneumonia.
evidence.explanation: Recurrent pneumonia is a presenting opportunistic illness in untreated SCID.

steps/25.description: Recurrent and opportunistic pneumonia, including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, is common.

evidence.snippet: Clinical manifestations are characterised by recurrent and severe bacterial, viral, and fungal opportunistic infections that start from early infancy period.
evidence.explanation: Recurrent fungal opportunistic infections are part of the SCID clinical picture.

steps/26.description: Persistent fungal infection, especially mucocutaneous candidiasis, reflects loss of T-cell immunity.

evidence.snippet: Clinical manifestations are characterised by recurrent and severe bacterial, viral, and fungal opportunistic infections that start from early infancy period.
evidence.explanation: Persistent fungal (candidal) infection including oral thrush reflects the T-cell immune defect in SCID.

steps/27.description: Persistent oral thrush is a frequent early manifestation of defective cellular immunity.

evidence.snippet: poor linear growth and weight gain secondary to persistent diarrhea
evidence.explanation: Persistent diarrhea is a frequent presenting feature contributing to failure to thrive in SCID.

steps/28.description: Persistent diarrhea, often from opportunistic enteric infection, is a common presenting feature.

evidence.snippet: Untreated ADA-SCID presents as life-threatening opportunistic illnesses in the first weeks to months of life with poor linear growth and weight gain secondary to persistent diarrhea
evidence.explanation: Poor linear growth and weight gain (failure to thrive) follow chronic infection and diarrhea in untreated SCID.

steps/29.description: Poor linear growth and weight gain secondary to chronic infection and persistent diarrhea.

evidence.snippet: Patients with typical SCID must have less than 0.05 × 109 autologous T cells/L on repetitive testing
evidence.explanation: Typical SCID is defined by profoundly low autologous T-cell counts.

steps/30.description: Profound T lymphocytopenia (<0.05 x 10^9 autologous T cells/L in typical SCID).

evidence.snippet: Characteristic immune abnormalities are lymphocytopenia (low numbers of T, B, and NK cells)
evidence.explanation: In T-B-NK- forms such as ADA-SCID, B-cell numbers are reduced along with T and NK cells.

steps/31.description: B lymphocytes are absent in T-B- forms (RAG1/RAG2, ADA, Artemis) and preserved in T-B+ forms.

evidence.snippet: Characteristic immune abnormalities are lymphocytopenia (low numbers of T, B, and NK cells)
evidence.explanation: NK-cell numbers are reduced in the NK-negative SCID immunophenotypes.

steps/32.description: NK cells are absent in T-B+NK- forms (IL2RG, JAK3) and in T-B-NK- ADA deficiency.

evidence.snippet: hypoplasia of secondary lymphoid organs and thymus
evidence.explanation: Documents thymic hypoplasia (rather than aplasia) as the thymic finding in SCID.

evidence.snippet: Deficiency of Coronin 1A known to result in T-B + SCID with a normal sized thymus.
evidence.explanation: Documents a SCID genotype with a normal-sized thymus, showing the thymic finding is genotype-dependent and not universal.

steps/33.description: A small, dysplastic thymus depleted of developing thymocytes produces the characteristic absent thymic shadow on chest imaging.

evidence.snippet: Omenn syndrome requires a generalized erythematous rash, absent transplacentally acquired maternal engraftment, and 2 or more of these: eosinophilia, elevated IgE, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly.
evidence.explanation: Hepatosplenomegaly is a recognized feature of the Omenn syndrome presentation of leaky SCID (RAG hypomorphs).

steps/34.description: Hepatosplenomegaly occurs particularly in Omenn syndrome and with disseminated infection.

evidence.snippet: Reticular dysgenesis is the most serious type of SCID that is associated with absent granulocytes, lymphocytes, hypoplasia of the primary and secondary lymphoid organs and fatal septicemia within days after birth.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents absent granulocytes in reticular dysgenesis.

steps/35.description: Absent granulocytes with profound neutropenia is the feature that separates reticular dysgenesis from every other SCID subtype, and follows from the haematopoietic-precursor rather than lymphoid-specific block.

evidence.snippet: Skeletal abnormalities affecting ribs and vertebra, pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, hemolytic anemia, neurologic abnormalities, and transaminitis may also suggest untreated ADA-SCID.
evidence.explanation: Lists pulmonary alveolar proteinosis among the extra-immune features suggestive of untreated ADA-SCID.

steps/36.description: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis is a recognized non-infectious pulmonary complication of untreated ADA deficiency.

evidence.snippet: Patients with ADA-SCID consistently achieve IQ scores that are not only below the population average but also below that of other SCID groups
evidence.explanation: Documents the cognitive deficit and its specificity to ADA deficiency within SCID, which is what makes it an extra-immune feature rather than a consequence of being a transplanted SCID patient.

steps/37.description: ADA-SCID patients score below the population average on IQ testing and also below other SCID groups receiving the same transplant treatment, and total IQ correlates inversely with the dATP level measured at diagnosis. That dissociation from the shared treatment is the argument that the deficit is metabolic rather than an artefact of transplantation.

evidence.snippet: ADA-SCID patients exhibit hyperactivity, attention deficits, aggressive behavior, and social problems, scoring abnormally in all of these areas of behavior
evidence.explanation: Names the behavioural abnormalities this phenotype records.

steps/38.description: Hyperactivity, attention deficit, aggression and social difficulty are reported across ADA-SCID cohorts, and track with the cognitive deficit: patients with lower IQ show more emotional and behavioural difficulty.

evidence.snippet: a 58% incidence was reported in the 12 patients who had undergone audiologic assessment in a study by Albuquerque and Gaspar
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the sensorineural deafness incidence in ADA-SCID that this phenotype records, and names the cohort it was measured in.

steps/39.description: Bilateral sensorineural deafness is reported as a non-immunological manifestation of ADA deficiency. In an audiologically assessed ADA-SCID transplant cohort the incidence was 58%, against 6% in patients transplanted for immunodeficiencies confined to the immune system; affected children had no identifiable genetic, structural, drug or infective cause, and some were transplanted without conditioning.

evidence.snippet: It is common for patients with ADA deficiency to display costochondral abnormalities and skeletal dysplasia
evidence.explanation: Documents the skeletal finding in patients that this phenotype records.

evidence.snippet: Skeletal abnormalities affecting ribs and vertebra, pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, hemolytic anemia, neurologic abnormalities, and transaminitis may also suggest untreated ADA-SCID.
evidence.explanation: Independent GeneReviews confirmation that rib and vertebral abnormality is part of the untreated ADA-SCID picture.

steps/40.description: Costochondral abnormality and skeletal dysplasia are commonly seen in ADA deficiency. Autopsy shows short growth plates with few proliferating and some hypertrophic chondrocytes, and ADA-deficient mice show reduced bone formation from impaired osteoblast function that neonatal enzyme replacement, transplant or gene therapy can correct.

evidence.snippet: elevated serum transaminase levels may be seen in patients with ADA deficiency: this is indicative of liver damage and often etiology is unknown
evidence.explanation: Documents the transaminase elevation in patients that this phenotype records.

evidence.snippet: the effects in ADA-deficient patients are not perinatally lethal and hepatic dysfunction has rarely been reported
evidence.explanation: Supports the rarity qualifier this phenotype's notes record, keeping the hepatic arm from reading as an established frequent feature.

steps/41.description: Elevated serum transaminases of frequently unknown aetiology are reported in ADA deficiency, and hyperbilirubinaemia, hepatitis, liver stiffness, fatty liver and hepatomegaly have each been described in individual patients, with resolution on enzyme replacement.

edges/13.description: Loss of IL-7/JAK-STAT signaling halts thymocyte survival and proliferation, blocking maturation of T lymphocytes.

edges/14.description: Failure of antigen-receptor gene recombination arrests thymocyte maturation, blocking T-cell development.

edges/15.description: Lymphotoxic deoxyadenosine/dATP accumulation impairs thymocyte survival and blocks T-cell development.

evidence.snippet: there is now a growing body of evidence that deficiency of ADA has significant impact on non-immunological organ systems
evidence.explanation: States the review's central claim, which is what this edge asserts: that the metabolic lesion has consequences outside the immune system.

evidence.snippet: Skeletal abnormalities affecting ribs and vertebra, pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, hemolytic anemia, neurologic abnormalities, and transaminitis may also suggest untreated ADA-SCID.
evidence.explanation: Enumerates the non-lymphoid organ systems this branch leads to, from the GeneReviews clinical description rather than from the review.

edges/16.description: ADA is expressed ubiquitously rather than only in lymphoid tissue, so the same accumulating metabolites reach cells that have no immunological role. This is the branch that makes ADA deficiency the one SCID subtype in this entry whose pathology is not confined to the immune system.

evidence.snippet: a significant inverse correlation between dATP levels at diagnosis and total IQ has been demonstrated
evidence.explanation: Ties the cognitive outcome to the accumulating metabolite rather than to treatment, which is what makes this a causal edge from this node.

edges/17.description: Adenosine is a CNS neuromodulator and ADA-SCID patients score below both the population average and other SCID groups on IQ, with an inverse correlation between diagnostic dATP level and total IQ. The intervening steps between metabolite accumulation and the cognitive deficit are not established.

evidence.snippet: ADA-SCID patients exhibit hyperactivity, attention deficits, aggressive behavior, and social problems, scoring abnormally in all of these areas of behavior
evidence.explanation: Reports the behavioural abnormalities this edge terminates in.

edges/18.description: The behavioural phenotype travels with the cognitive one and is reported in the same cohorts, with lower IQ accompanied by more behavioural difficulty.

evidence.snippet: bilateral sensorineural deafness has been investigated as a non-immunological manifestation of ADA deficiency
evidence.explanation: States the attribution of the auditory phenotype to the metabolic lesion rather than to the immunodeficiency or its treatment.

edges/19.description: Bilateral sensorineural deafness occurs at roughly ten times the rate seen after transplant for immunodeficiencies confined to the immune system, in children with no structural, genetic, drug or infective cause, including children transplanted without conditioning.

evidence.snippet: It is common for patients with ADA deficiency to display costochondral abnormalities and skeletal dysplasia
evidence.explanation: Reports the skeletal phenotype in patients that this edge terminates in.

evidence.snippet: it is unknown whether these bony defects are caused by the disrupted purine metabolism or the underlying immunodeficiency
evidence.explanation: Withholds the attribution this edge makes: the same review states the causal assignment to purine metabolism is not settled for bone.

edges/20.description: Costochondral abnormality and skeletal dysplasia are common in ADA deficiency, and ADA-deficient mice show reduced bone formation from impaired osteoblast function. Whether the human bone phenotype follows from the purine lesion or from the immunodeficiency is explicitly unresolved, so this edge is the weakest of the five.

evidence.snippet: elevated serum transaminase levels may be seen in patients with ADA deficiency: this is indicative of liver damage and often etiology is unknown
evidence.explanation: Reports the hepatic laboratory abnormality in patients that this edge terminates in, and records that its aetiology is often unestablished.

edges/21.description: Hepatic involvement is the thinnest arm of the human evidence — transaminase elevation of unknown aetiology is reported but hepatic dysfunction is rare in patients, while ADA-deficient mice die perinatally of hepatocyte degeneration.

evidence.snippet: The incidence of ADA-deficient patients with PAP was reported to be 43.8% in this Grunebaum study
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the PAP incidence specific to ADA deficiency that this edge asserts follows from the metabolic lesion.

edges/22.description: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis occurred in 43.8% of ADA-deficient patients and in none of the patients with other forms of SCID, with no clinical or immunological difference between the ADA patients who developed it and those who did not — which is what places it on this branch rather than on the infectious consequences of the immunodeficiency.

edges/23.description: Failure of haematopoietic precursor survival removes the progenitors from which thymocytes would derive.

edges/24.description: The same precursor-survival defect abolishes granulocyte production, a myeloid consequence absent from the other SCID subtypes.

edges/25.description: Absent haematopoietic precursors leave the primary and secondary lymphoid organs hypoplastic.

edges/26.description: Without a signalling-competent T-cell receptor complex, or without the adaptor that carries its signal onward, beta-selection cannot be driven and thymocyte maturation arrests before the double-positive stage.

edges/27.description: Thymocytes that cannot leave the thymus, and peripheral T cells that do not survive, leave the periphery without a functional T-cell compartment even though intrathymic development is not itself arrested.

edges/28.description: Absence of functional T lymphocytes abolishes cell-mediated immunity and (directly or via loss of T-cell help) humoral immunity.

edges/29.description: Blocked thymic T-cell development produces profound T lymphocytopenia.

edges/30.description: Absence of developing thymocytes leaves a small, dysplastic thymus that yields an absent thymic shadow on imaging.

edges/31.description: In T-B- subtypes (RAG1/RAG2, Artemis, ADA) the same developmental/metabolic block also abolishes B-lymphocyte development.

edges/32.description: In NK-negative subtypes (IL2RG, JAK3, ADA) the gamma-chain signaling or metabolic defect also abolishes NK-cell development.

edges/33.description: Loss of adaptive immunity is the defining clinical immunodeficiency.

edges/34.description: Loss of functional T cells abolishes cell-mediated immune responses.

edges/35.description: Without adaptive immunity, infants suffer recurrent and persistent infections from early infancy.

edges/36.description: Loss of T-cell immunity predisposes to fungal infection including persistent candidiasis.

edges/37.description: Defective cellular immunity allows persistent oral Candida infection.

edges/38.description: Loss of adaptive immunity predisposes to recurrent and opportunistic pneumonia (including Pneumocystis).

edges/39.description: Opportunistic enteric infection and immune dysfunction produce persistent diarrhea.

edges/40.description: Chronic infection and diarrhea cause poor linear growth and weight gain.

edges/41.description: Disseminated infection and immune dysregulation (e.g., Omenn syndrome) can produce hepatosplenomegaly.

evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of typical and atypical X-SCID is established in a male proband with suggestive findings and a hemizygous pathogenic variant in IL2RG identified by molecular genetic testing.
evidence.explanation: A hemizygous IL2RG pathogenic variant establishes the diagnosis of X-linked SCID.

evidence.snippet: The gamma portion of IL2R is important for the development of T and NK cells through cytokines IL2 and IL15, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Explains why common gamma-chain loss removes both T and NK lineages, giving the T-B+NK- immunophenotype.

evidence.snippet: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency is a systemic purine metabolic disorder that primarily affects lymphocyte development, viability, and function.
evidence.explanation: Biallelic ADA deficiency causes a systemic purine metabolic disorder affecting lymphocyte development, the basis of ADA-SCID.

evidence.snippet: The ADA deficiency phenotypic spectrum includes typical early-onset severe combined immunodeficiency (ADA-SCID), diagnosed in infancy (about 80% of individuals), and less severe "delayed" or "late-onset" combined immunodeficiency (ADA-CID), diagnosed in older children and adults (15%-20% of individuals).
evidence.explanation: Supports the "about 80%" typical-SCID proportion stated in these features.

evidence.snippet: Deficiency of either RAG1 or RAG2 causes T-B-NK + SCID and is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
evidence.explanation: RAG1 deficiency is a well-characterized autosomal recessive cause of T-B-NK+ SCID via a V(D)J-recombination defect.

evidence.snippet: RAG1 and RAG2, are DNA recombinases that mediate DNA recombination process and ensure the somatic diversification of immunoglobulin and TCR genes during B-cell and T-cell development, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Supports the specific molecular role — recombinase-driven antigen-receptor gene diversification — asserted in these features.

evidence.snippet: Deficiency of either RAG1 or RAG2 causes T-B-NK + SCID and is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
evidence.explanation: RAG2 deficiency, like RAG1, abolishes V(D)J recombination and causes autosomal recessive T-B-NK+ SCID.

evidence.snippet: Deficiency of ILR7 alpha causes T-B + NK + SCID, that accounts for around 10% of the total SCID patients.
evidence.explanation: IL7R (IL7R alpha) deficiency selectively impairs T-cell development, producing a T-B+NK+ form accounting for about 10% of SCID.

evidence.snippet: The encoded protein is expressed on the lymphoid lineage and is required during T cell development during early stage and for proliferation and survival of T cells in the periphery.
evidence.explanation: Supports the specific requirement for IL-7 receptor alpha in early T-cell development and peripheral T-cell survival.

evidence.snippet: JAK3 deficiency constitutes around 6% of the total SCID patients and is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
evidence.explanation: JAK3 deficiency is an autosomal recessive SCID acting downstream of the common gamma chain, accounting for about 6% of cases.

evidence.snippet: RAG2 (17), JAK3 (15), DCLRE1C (13), IL7RA (9)
evidence.explanation: A multi-institutional cohort identifies DCLRE1C (Artemis) defects as a recurrent molecular cause of SCID.

evidence.snippet: DCLRE1C encodes ARTEMIS, a nuclease which is single-stranded with- 5′-3′ exonuclease potential and endonuclease activity over 5′ and 3′ ends. It is essential for V(D)J rearrangement and for DNA repair.
evidence.explanation: Supports the dual V(D)J-rearrangement and DNA-repair role asserted in these features.

evidence.snippet: Artemis deficiency causes early arrest in the maturation of T cells and B cell differentiation during early pre-B cell stage, resulting in T–B–NK + SCID.
evidence.explanation: Supports the T-B-NK+ immunophenotype attributed to Artemis deficiency.

evidence.snippet: Patients with this form of SCID are sensitive to ionizing radiation and chemotherapeutic agents.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports the radiosensitivity claim, which the previously cited gene-count snippet did not address.

evidence.snippet: Mutation of the AK2 gene causes reticular dysgenesis (RD), an autosomal recessive disorder occurring in 2% of children with SCID.
evidence.explanation: Establishes AK2 as causative for reticular dysgenesis and its frequency among SCID.

evidence.snippet: Deficiency of AK2 is associated with lack of innate and adaptive immunity.
evidence.explanation: Supports the combined innate-plus-adaptive failure that distinguishes AK2 deficiency from the lymphoid-restricted SCID subtypes.

evidence.snippet: Adenylate kinases are involved in cellular and mitochondrial energy homeostasis.
evidence.explanation: Supports the non-lymphoid-specific, bioenergetic function of AK2 asserted in these features.

evidence.snippet: Radiosensitive T-B- severe combined immunodeficiency (RS-SCID) is caused by defects in the nonhomologous end-joining (NHEJ) DNA repair pathway, which results in failure of functional V(D)J recombination.
evidence.explanation: Places DNA-PKcs deficiency in the NHEJ/V(D)J mechanism class this entry already models, and gives the T-B-NK+ immunophenotype.

evidence.snippet: Here we have identified the first human RS-SCID patient to our knowledge with a DNA-PKcs missense mutation (L3062R).
evidence.explanation: Establishes PRKDC as a human SCID gene rather than only a mouse one.

evidence.snippet: DNA ligase IV functions in DNA nonhomologous end-joining and V(D)J recombination.
evidence.explanation: States the molecular step at which LIG4 acts, which is the node this gene is wired to.

evidence.snippet: Cell lines from the patients show pronounced radiosensitivity.
evidence.explanation: Sources the cellular radiosensitivity that groups LIG4 with Artemis and DNA-PKcs for conditioning purposes.

evidence.snippet: This study enrolled seven Chinese patients with LIG4 deficiency who presented with combined immunodeficiency, microcephaly, and growth retardation.
evidence.explanation: Sources the microcephaly and growth retardation recorded in these features, and the cohort in which the combined immunodeficiency was characterized.

evidence.snippet: Patients with hypomorphic mutations in LIG4 present with a range of phenotypes, from normal to severe combined immunodeficiency.
evidence.explanation: Sources the phenotypic range recorded in these notes, which is why LIG4 is bound as a gene at the DNA repair node rather than asserted as a SCID subtype.

genes/9.notes: Bound here as a gene acting at the V(D)J recombination and DNA repair node, not as a subtype row. The IUIS 2022 classification lists DNA ligase IV deficiency in the T-B- SCID table, but the disease-specific review describes a phenotypic range from normal to severe combined immunodeficiency, so treating LIG4 syndrome as a SCID subtype in its own right would overstate a variable immune phenotype in a disorder whose defining features are radiosensitivity and microcephaly. The review cited below states that range directly.

evidence.snippet: Homozygous mutations in CD3D and CD3E genes lead to a complete block in T-cell development and thus to an early-onset severe combined immunodeficiency phenotype.
evidence.explanation: Establishes CD3D as a SCID gene and states the complete developmental block this node asserts.

evidence.snippet: Thymic studies have shown that the defect in T-cell development occurs at the transition between 'double-negative' and 'double-positive' thymocytes.
evidence.explanation: Locates the arrest at beta-selection, the step this node places downstream of receptor-proximal signalling failure.

evidence.snippet: Linker for activation of T cells (LAT) is a transmembrane adaptor signaling molecule that is part of the TCR complex and essential for T-cell development, as demonstrated by LAT-deficient mice, which show a complete lack of peripheral T cells.
evidence.explanation: States that LAT is a component of the TCR complex required for T-cell development, which is the mechanism this gene is bound to.

evidence.snippet: We describe a pedigree affected by a severe combined immunodeficiency phenotype with absent T cells and normal B-cell and natural killer cell numbers.
evidence.explanation: Sources the human SCID phenotype and its T-B+NK+ immunophenotype.

evidence.snippet: Our findings establish a function for coronin 1A in T cell egress, identify a surface of coronin involved in Arp2/3 regulation and demonstrate that actin regulation is a biological process defective in human and mouse severe combined immunodeficiency.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the egress mechanism and that coronin-1A loss is a human SCID mechanism distinct from the four already modelled here.

evidence.snippet: Whereas complete absence of coronin 1A is associated with severe combined immunodeficiency in humans, hypomorphic mutations lead to a profound defect in naïve T cells, expansion of oligoclonal memory T cells, and exquisite susceptibility to EBV-associated B cell lymphoproliferation.
evidence.explanation: Sources the allele-dependent split recorded in these features, which is why this gene is not asserted as a uniform SCID subtype.

genes/12.notes: Neither cited report states the size of the human thymus, so no thymic-size claim is made for this gene.

evidence.snippet: Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is the treatment of choice.
evidence.explanation: HSCT is the curative treatment of choice for SCID.

evidence.snippet: overall SCID survival was 45 of 52 (87%), while 45 of 49 treated infants (92%) survived
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the survival achieved when SCID is detected by newborn screening and treated early, supporting the claim that outcomes are best when transplant precedes infection.

evidence.snippet: radiosensitive forms of SCID are prone to develop increased toxicity to alkylator-based chemotherapeutic agents used in the conditioning regimen for HSCT
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the treatment: the conditioning regimen must be adapted in radiosensitive genotypes, so HSCT is not uniformly deliverable across SCID subtypes.

evidence.snippet: Pre-transplant conditioning regimens are preferably avoided in patients with radiosensitive forms of SCID.
evidence.explanation: States the genotype-specific management consequence recorded in this treatment's notes.

treatments/0.description: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the definitive curative treatment for SCID, reconstituting a functional immune system; outcomes are best when performed early, before the onset of infections.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Donor hematopoietic stem cells reconstitute thymic T-cell development and adaptive immunity.

evidence.snippet: Long-term persistence of multilineage gene-corrected cells, metabolic detoxification, immune reconstitution and decreased infection rates were observed.
evidence.explanation: Retroviral hematopoietic stem cell gene therapy provides durable multilineage engraftment, immune reconstitution, and reduced infections in ADA-SCID.

evidence.snippet: 2 years intervention-free survival (no need for long-term enzyme replacement therapy or allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation) of 88% (95% confidence interval 78.7-98.4%)
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the durability of the benefit — the proportion of treated patients needing neither ongoing ERT nor rescue allogeneic transplant.

evidence.snippet: One patient from the named patient program developed a T cell leukemia related to treatment 4.7 years after GT and is currently in remission.
evidence.explanation: Records the insertional-oncogenesis risk of retroviral gene therapy — a treatment-related leukaemia in the long-term cohort — so the entry does not present gene therapy as risk-free.

treatments/1.description: Autologous hematopoietic stem cell gene therapy corrects the causative gene in the patient's own stem cells; it is an established alternative to allogeneic HSCT for ADA-SCID (Strimvelis) and has shown clinical success for X-linked and other SCID forms.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Gene-corrected autologous stem cells restore lymphocyte development and adaptive immunity.

evidence.snippet: enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) by intramuscular administration of PEGylated ADA
evidence.explanation: Enzyme replacement therapy with PEGylated ADA is a targeted treatment correcting the ADA metabolic defect.

evidence.snippet: Often, ERT is initiated first to rapidly correct the metabolic defect and to protect against serious infections as well as neurologic/behavioral abnormalities. It is discontinued at the time HSCT or HSC-GT is performed.
evidence.explanation: Supports the bridging role asserted in this treatment's description, and specifies that ERT is stopped once curative therapy is delivered rather than continued alongside it.

treatments/2.description: For ADA deficiency, enzyme replacement therapy with PEGylated adenosine deaminase corrects the metabolic defect, providing protection against infection; it is often used to stabilize patients before curative HSCT or gene therapy.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Exogenous PEGylated ADA clears toxic deoxyadenosine/adenosine, correcting the lymphotoxic metabolic defect.

evidence.snippet: use of immunoglobulin infusions and antibiotics, particularly prophylaxis against Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
evidence.explanation: Immunoglobulin infusions are an explicit part of supportive management for the profound antibody deficiency seen in SCID.

treatments/3.description: Intravenous (or subcutaneous) immunoglobulin replacement provides passive humoral protection while patients await or recover from definitive immune reconstitution.

evidence.snippet: particularly prophylaxis against Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (formerly Pneumocystis carinii) and fungal infections
evidence.explanation: Prophylaxis against Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia is a standard supportive measure in SCID.

treatments/4.description: Antimicrobial prophylaxis, particularly against Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, is a standard supportive measure to prevent opportunistic infection pending immune reconstitution.

evidence.snippet: live viral vaccines for the affected individual as well as household contacts; transfusion of non-irradiated blood products
evidence.explanation: Names the two exposures this treatment exists to prevent, including the household-contact extension of the live-vaccine restriction.

evidence.snippet: All infants with T-cell lymphopenia were directed to avoid infectious exposures, transfusions (except with cytomegalovirus-negative, irradiated blood products), and live rotavirus vaccines until such time as immune compromise was no longer present.
evidence.explanation: Documents this as applied practice across 11 newborn-screening programmes, including the CMV-negative irradiated-product qualifier and the live-rotavirus-vaccine restriction.

treatments/5.description: Until immune reconstitution is achieved, exposure avoidance is itself treatment. Live viral vaccines — given to the infant or to household contacts — can cause disseminated vaccine-strain disease; non-irradiated blood products can cause transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease in a patient with no T cells to reject donor lymphocytes; and breast milk is withheld pending maternal CMV status. Live rotavirus vaccine is the specific exposure that newborn-screening programmes act on first, because it is administered at the age at which screened infants are still awaiting definitive therapy.

evidence.snippet: Current research has not, so far, investigated the mechanism of pathology. One possibility is that the accumulation of dATP causes neurotoxic effects by a similar mechanism elucidated in the immune system
evidence.explanation: States the gap directly: the mechanism of the CNS pathology is uninvestigated, and the immune-system analogy is offered as a hypothesis.

evidence.snippet: neurological abnormalities are far more prevalent in ADA-SCID than other forms of immunodeficiency
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the gap is about a real, ADA-specific phenomenon rather than a general consequence of severe immunodeficiency or its treatment.
